# 5. MyBatis, Spring, Altibase Integration
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/5.+MyBatis%2C+Spring%2C+Altibase+Integration
Updated: 2025-10-21T09:30:39.000+0900

- [Setting dataSource by integrating MyBatis into Spring](#id-5.MyBatis,Spring,AltibaseIntegration-SettingdataSourcebyintegratingMyBatisintoSpring) - [How to Configure Connection Pool](#id-5.MyBatis,Spring,AltibaseIntegration-HowtoConfigureConnectionPool)

To integrate MyBatis and Spring with Altibase, you need to define the dataSource in Spring using the MyBatis module and connect it to Altibase.

This chapter explains how to connect Altibase using the MyBatis module in Spring.

## Setting dataSource by integrating MyBatis into Spring

---

To use Altibase together with Spring and MyBatis, configure the following in Spring’s configuration file (applicationContext.xml):

- SqlSessionFactory bean using the MyBatis module
- Transaction settings via transactionManager
- DataSource for the database
- Mapper Bean configuration: To perform the integration, you need the MyBatis-Spring integration modules, which are named as follows:

- mybatis-spring-1.x.x.jar: Using the mybatis-spring integration module requires Java version 1.5 or higher. Note that MyBatis and Spring versions may vary slightly depending on their releases. Please refer to the table below for detailed version compatibility information

| MyBatis Spring Integration Modules | MyBatis | Spring |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 | 3.0.1 to 3.0.5 | 3.0.0 or higher |
| 1.0.2 | 3.0.6 | 3.0.0 or higher |
| 1.1.0 or higher | 3.1.0 or higher | 3.0.0 or higher |

To use MyBatis together with Spring, you need to specify the MyBatis SqlSessionFactory bean and Mapper bean in Spring’s ApplicationContext.xml file.

The Mapper bean defines the methods that actually handle the queries, and it is processed via interfaces in the Spring framework.

In an environment integrating MyBatis and Spring, to configure the dataSource in Spring, you select one of the methods described in the 『Altibase_Spring_Integration_Guide』 document and specify the DB’s datasource name in the dataSource property of the SqlSessionFactory bean and TransactionManager bean.

Below is an example of specifying the dataSource, SqlSessionFactory bean, and TransactionManager bean in the applicationContext.xml file.

Example) ApplicationContext.xml file of altibase_mybatis_spring

```
…
<!-- DataSource configuration using the DriverManagerDataSource class -->
<bean id="dataSource" class="org.springframework.jdbc.datasource.DriverManagerDataSource">
   <property name="driverClassName" value="Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver" />
   <property name="url" value="jdbc:Altibase://192.168.1.35:36492/mydb" />
   <property name="username" value="sys" />
   <property name="password" value="manager" />
</bean>
…
<!-- TransactionManager bean configuration -->
<bean id= TransactionManager "
class="org.springframework.jdbc.datasource.DataSourceTransactionManager">
<property name="dataSource" ref="dataSource" />
</bean>
…
<!-- SqlSessionFactory bean configuration -->
<bean id="SqlSessionFactory" class="org.mybatis.spring.SqlSessionFactoryBean">
<property name="dataSource" ref="dataSource" />
<property name="typeAliasesPackage" value="com.altibase.test.domain" />
</bean>
```

This example is based on a Spring Template Project and was created using Maven. The libraries that users need to add are only the DB connection library (Altibase.jar), MyBatis-related library (mybatis-3.2.8.jar), and MyBatis-Spring integration library (mybatis-spring-1.2.1.jar). Spring-related libraries are handled automatically via Maven.

(The project was created using Spring MVC within the Spring Template Project, and when created this way, the generated pom.xml file automatically imports the necessary libraries using the dependency tags. Detailed information is provided in the appendix.)

![eclipse_jdbc_setting4.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/5.%20MyBatis,%20Spring,%20Altibase%20Integration/eclipse_jdbc_setting4.png?api=v2)

## How to Configure Connection Pool

---

With Spring-MyBatis integration, the dataSource configuration can be set independently. Note that without Spring integration, MyBatis alone cannot use connection pools from other modules; you must integrate with Spring to use connection pools from other modules.

Below is an example of configuring a Connection Pool.

Example) applicationContext.xml file of altibase_mybatis_spring

```
...
<!—Altibase Connection Pool-->
<bean id="dataSource" class="Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseConnectionPoolDataSource">
	<property name="URL" value="jdbc:Altibase://192.168.1.62:21020/mydb" />
	<property name="user" value="test" />
	<property name="password" value="test" />
</bean>
...

<!—Apache Connection Pool-->
<bean id="dataSource"
class="org.apache.commons.dbcp.BasicDataSource" destroy-method="close">
<property name="driverClassName" value="Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver" />
<property name="url" value="jdbc:Altibase://192.168.1.35:36492/mydb" />
<property name="username" value="sys" />
<property name="password" value="manager" />
<property name="initialSize" value="10" />
<property name="minIdle" value="25" />
<property name="maxIdle" value="30" />
<property name="maxActive" value="100" />
<property name="validationQuery" value="select 1 from dual" />
</bean>
```
<!-- SOURCE_BLOCK_END source_id="AID-SRC-000361" block_id="BLOCK-000370" -->

# 6. Transaction Management
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/6.+Transaction+Management
Updated: 2025-10-21T09:31:06.000+0900

- [Transaction Management in MyBatis](#id-6.TransactionManagement-TransactionManagementinMyBatis)

When integrating MyBatis with a database, the dataSource is specified in the <transactionManager> tag within each DB-specific <environment> under the <environments> section of the Configuration file. The database connection is then established through the SqlSessionFactory object using the <environment> id. At this time, auto-commit mode can also be configured, with the default being auto-commit enabled.

This chapter introduces various transaction management methods.

## Transaction Management in MyBatis

---

Unlike iBatis, where only one DB could be configured per configuration file, MyBatis allows multiple DBs to be configured and managed under the <environments> tag.

Each <environment> tag within <environments> configures one DB, specifying the dataSource under the <transactionManager> tag. The application programmer can manage transactions directly.

In MyBatis, there is no explicit transaction start or end. Instead, auto-commit mode can be set when configuring the SqlSessionFactory through the Configuration.

The following example shows how to configure multiple DBs in a single Configuration file. Example) mybatis-config.xml file of altibase_mybatis_MultiVersionConnection

```
…
<!-- DB connection options: UNPOOLED/POOLED/JNDI -->
<!-- transactionManager options: JDBC/MANAGED -->
<environments default="development">
<!-- connection configuration for the development alias (version 5) -->
<environment id="development">
  <transactionManager type="JDBC" />
  <dataSource type="POOLED">
    <property name="driver" value="${jdbc5.driver}" />
    <property name="url" value="${jdbc5.url}" />
    <property name="username" value="${jdbc5.username}" />
    <property name="password" value="${jdbc5.password}" />
    <property name="poolPingQuery" value="select 1 from dual"/>
      <property name="poolMaximumActiveConnections" value="100"/>
      <property name="poolMaximumIdleConnections" value="50"/>
      <property name="poolMaximumCheckoutTime" value="20000"/>
  </dataSource>
</environment>
<!-- connection configuration for the release alias (version 6 or later) -->
  <environment id="release">
    <transactionManager type="JDBC" />
    <dataSource type="POOLED">
      <property name="driver" value="${jdbc.driver}" />
      <property name="url" value="${jdbc.url}" />
      <property name="username" value="${jdbc.username}" />
      <property name="password" value="${jdbc.password}" />
      <property name="poolPingQuery" value="select 1 from dual"/>
        <property name="poolMaximumActiveConnections" value="100"/>
        <property name="poolMaximumIdleConnections" value="50"/>
        <property name="poolMaximumCheckoutTime" value="20000"/>
    </dataSource>
  </environment>
</environments>
…
```

Example) MybatisUtil.java file of altibase_mybatis_MultiVersionConnection

```
…
// Read configuration values from mybatis-config.xml
inputStream = Resources.getResourceAsStream("mybatis-config.xml");
// Create a SqlSessionFactory from the XML file. Pass the environment id as an argument to select the DB configuration.
sqlSessionFactory = new SqlSessionFactoryBuilder()build(inputStream, “release”);
// Create a SqlSession object. The argument determines whether autoCommit is enabled.
// The default is true. Passing false sets autocommit=false.
sqlSession = sqlSessionFactory.openSession(false);
…
```

To run the above altibase_mybatis_MultiVersionConnection project example, just like setting the dataSource in the Configuration file to connect with ALTIBASE, the Altibase.jar and mybatis-3.2.8.jar files are required.

# 7. Considerations for MyBatis Integration
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/7.+Considerations+for+MyBatis+Integration
Updated: 2025-10-21T09:31:34.000+0900

This chapter describes considerations when integrating Altibase with MyBatis.

## LOB Data Handling

---

In iBatis, to handle LOBs, it was necessary to explicitly specify the jdbcType as CLOB or BLOB in the Mapper file’s parameter and result settings, typically using parameterMap. However, since parameterMap is deprecated in MyBatis, you now directly specify the jdbcType on the columns being bound in the query. If jdbcType is not explicitly specified, the data will not be recognized as LOB and will cause an error.

Below is an example showing the parameterMap and resultMap settings for CLOB type data.

Example) LobMapper.xml (Mapper) file of altibase_mybatis_lob

```
<mapper namespace="com.altibase.psy.mapper.LobMapper">
<!-- LOB select, insert, update, delete Test - 2013/11/05 -->
<select id="selectBlobData" parameterType="Integer" resultType="LobVo">
	SELECT user_no as userNo, user_name as userName, blob_data as blobData, clob_data as clobData, reg_date as regDate
	FROM test_blob
	WHERE user_no = #{userNo}
</select>

<select id="selectAllBlobData"  resultType="LobVo">
	SELECT user_no as userNo, user_name as userName, blob_data as blobData, clob_data as clobData, reg_date as regDate
	FROM test_blob
</select>

<insert id="insertBlobData" parameterType="LobVo">
	insert into test_blob(user_no, user_name, blob_data, clob_data, reg_date)
	values(#{userNo}, #{userName}, #{blobData,jdbcType=BLOB}, #{clobData,jdbcType=CLOB}, #{regDate})
</insert>

<update id="updateBlobData" parameterType="LobVo">
	update test_blob set
		user_name = #{userName},
		blob_data = #{blobData,jdbcType=BLOB},
		clob_data = #{clobData,jdbcType=CLOB},
		reg_date = #{regDate}
	where user_no = #{userNo}
</update>
...

</mapper>
```

When handling LOBs, an important point to note is that Altibase requires autocommit mode to be set to false and transactions to be managed accordingly. In iBATIS integration, when dataSource is set in the <transactionManager> of the SqlMapConfig file, setAutoCommit(false) is internally called to disable autocommit, so no special consideration is needed for LOB handling. However, in MyBatis, the default is true, so it must be explicitly set when obtaining the session.

If autocommit mode is not set to false, an error like “java.sql.SQLException: [0]:LobLocator can not span the transaction 101858625.” will occur.

This error also occurs when inserting LOB data.

The following example is part of a sample that handles LOB data in MyBatis, with the full source attached in the appendix.

Example) LobMapper.xml file of altibase_mybatis_lob

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE mapper PUBLIC "-//mybatis.org//DTD Mapper 3.0//EN"
"http://mybatis.org/dtd/mybatis-3-mapper.dtd">

<mapper namespace="com.altibase.psy.mapper.LobMapper">
	<!-- LOB select, insert, update, delete Test - 2013/11/05 -->
	<select id="selectBlobData" parameterType="Integer" resultType="LobVo">
		SELECT user_no as userNo, user_name as userName, blob_data as blobData, clob_data as clobData, reg_date as regDate
		FROM test_blob
		WHERE user_no = #{userNo}
	</select>

	<select id="selectAllBlobData"  resultType="LobVo">
		SELECT user_no as userNo, user_name as userName, blob_data as blobData, clob_data as clobData, reg_date as regDate
		FROM test_blob
	</select>

	<insert id="insertBlobData" parameterType="LobVo">
		insert into test_blob(user_no, user_name, blob_data, clob_data, reg_date)
		values(#{userNo}, #{userName}, #{blobData,jdbcType=BLOB}, #{clobData,jdbcType=CLOB}, #{regDate})
	</insert>

	<update id="updateBlobData" parameterType="LobVo">
		update test_blob set
			user_name = #{userName},
			blob_data = #{blobData,jdbcType=BLOB},
			clob_data = #{clobData,jdbcType=CLOB},
			reg_date = #{regDate}
		where user_no = #{userNo}
	</update>

	<delete id="deleteBlobData" parameterType="Integer">
		delete from test_blob
		where user_no = #{userNo}
	</delete>

</mapper>
```

To run the above altibase_mybatis_lob project, the Altibase.jar and mybatis-3.2.8.jar files are required.

![eclipse_jdbc_setting5.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/7.%20Considerations%20for%20MyBatis%20Integration/eclipse_jdbc_setting5.png?api=v2)

## The issue of duplicate Insert queries being sent during Insert operations

---

```
15:15:55.076 [main] [main] [ERROR] - 2. Connection.prepareStatement(insert into TB_DB_CONFIGSET_LEVEL(DB_TYPE_CODE, LEVEL_CODE, LEVEL_NAME
      )
    values (?, ?, ?
      ), 1) insert into TB_DB_CONFIGSET_LEVEL(DB_TYPE_CODE, LEVEL_CODE, LEVEL_NAME
      )
    values (?, ?, ?
      )
```

Issue Description:

- When setting 'useGeneratedKeys' to true in the MyBatis configuration XML, the problem described above occurs.

- This setting is defined as follows ([http://mybatis.github.io/mybatis-3/ko/sqlmap-xml.html](http://mybatis.github.io/mybatis-3/ko/sqlmap-xml.html)):

- It enables the use of the JDBC getGeneratedKeys method to retrieve keys generated internally by the database.

- Default value: 'false'

- Changing this setting to false prevents the issue from occurring.

- This problem does not occur with Oracle or Informix databases with the same setting.
<!-- SOURCE_BLOCK_END source_id="AID-SRC-000363" block_id="BLOCK-000372" -->

# 8. Appendix 1 (MyBatis-Altibase Integration)
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=22643034
Updated: 2025-10-21T09:32:00.000+0900

- [Creating DB Table and Sequence](#id-8.Appendix1(MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-CreatingDBTableandSequence) - [Create Project](#id-8.Appendix1(MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-CreateProject) - [Package Naming Convention](#id-8.Appendix1(MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-PackageNamingConvention) - [Creating Configuration File](#id-8.Appendix1(MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-CreatingConfigurationFile) - [Create Mapper File](#id-8.Appendix1(MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-CreateMapperFile) - [Creating the Application](#id-8.Appendix1(MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-CreatingtheApplication) - [Add related JAR files](#id-8.Appendix1(MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-AddrelatedJARfiles) - [Run the Application](#id-8.Appendix1(MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-RuntheApplication)

Based on the altibase_mybatis_sidu example, this explains in more detail how to integrate MyBatis with ALTIBASE. Note that the IDE used is Eclipse.

## Creating DB Table and Sequence

---

Create the following table and sequence in the database.

```
create table users(
  user_no integer,
  user_name varchar(30),
  user_content varchar(200),
  reg_date date
);
```

## Create Project

---

In Eclipse, create a project named altibase_mybatis_sidu.

1. Menu – File – Click Java Project
2. Enter Project name: Altibase_mybatis_sidu
3. Click the Finish button

![additional1.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/8.%20Appendix%201%20(MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional1.png?api=v2)

## Package Naming Convention

---

The package name explained in the appendix is basically named com.altibase.sidu, which follows common package classification rules. Each part has the following meaning:

- com: The first part defines the leading group of the project, where com stands for company. For smaller organizations, org (organization) might be used instead.

- altibase: The second part defines the company or group name. For companies, it’s usually the company name; for groups, the group name. Since this document is from Altibase, it is named altibase.

- sidu: The third part represents the artifact structure of this project. Since this sample covers general DML commands (Select/Insert/Delete/Update), it is named sidu.

## Creating Configuration File

---

1. Create a properties file (db.properties) that defines properties for connecting to Altibase.

(In the altibase_mybatis_sidu project – right-click the src directory, select New – File, and name the file db.properties.)

```
jdbc.driver=Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver
jdbc.url=jdbc:Altibase://192.168.1.62:21020/mydb
jdbc.username=sys
jdbc.password=manager
```

2. In the configuration file (mybatis-config.xml), set the dataSource and SqlMap files for integration with ALTIBASE.

(In the altibase_mybatis_sidu project – right-click the src directory, click New – File, and name the file mybatis-config.xml.)

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE configuration PUBLIC "-//mybatis.org//DTD Config 3.0//EN"
"http://mybatis.org/dtd/mybatis-3-config.dtd">
<configuration>

<typeAliases>
	<typeAlias type="com.altibase.sidu.model.UserVo" alias="User" />
</typeAliases>

<environments default="development">
	<environment id="development">
		<transactionManager type="JDBC" />
		<dataSource type="SIMPLE">
			<property name="driver" value="${jdbc.driver}" />
			<property name="url" value="${jdbc.url}" />
			<property name="username" value="${jdbc.username}" />
			<property name="password" value="${jdbc.password}" />
			<property name="poolPingQuery" value="select 1 from dual" />
		</dataSource>
	</environment>
</environments>

<mappers>
	<mapper resource="com/altibase/sidu/mapper/UserMapper.xml" />
</mappers>

</configuration>
```

## Create Mapper File

---

Create a Mapper file (Person.xml) that defines methods mapped to CRUD SQL statements for the Users table.

The Mapper is created in the com.altibase.sidu.mapper package.

1. In the altibase_mybatis_sidu project – right-click the src directory, click New – Package, and create a new package named com.altibase.sidu.mapper.

![additional2.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/8.%20Appendix%201%20(MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2.png?api=v2)

2. In the newly created package (com.altibase.sidu.mapper), right-click, select New – File, and name the file UserMapper.xml.

![additional4.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/8.%20Appendix%201%20(MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional4.png?api=v2)

3. Write the following content into UserMapper.xml.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE mapper PUBLIC "-//mybatis.org//DTD Mapper 3.0//EN"
"http://mybatis.org/dtd/mybatis-3-mapper.dtd">

<mapper namespace="com.altibase.sidu.mapper.UserMapper">
	<select id="selectUserData" parameterType="Integer" resultType="User">
		SELECT user_no as userNo,
		user_name as userName,
		user_content as userContent,
		reg_date as regDate
		FROM users
		WHERE user_no = #{userNo}
	</select>

	<select id="selectAllUserData" resultType="User">
		SELECT user_no as userNo,
		user_name as userName,
		user_content as userContent,
		reg_date as regDate
		FROM users
	</select>

	<insert id="insertUserData" parameterType="User">
		insert into
		users(user_no, user_name, user_content, reg_date)
		values(#{userNo}, #{userName}, #{userContent}, #{regDate})
	</insert>

	<update id="updateUserData" parameterType="User">
		update users
		set user_name = #{userName},
		user_content = #{userContent},
		reg_date = #{regDate}
		where user_no = #{userNo}
	</update>

	<delete id="deleteUserData" parameterType="User">
		delete from users
		where user_no = #{userNo}
	</delete>
</mapper>
```

When the application calls the insert, update, or delete methods in the configuration, the SQL statements defined in the <insert>, <update>, <delete>, and <select> tags with matching ids in the above file are automatically executed.

## Creating the Application

---

1. Create a VO (Value Object) class for the users table called UserVO (UserVo.java). 1-1. In the altibase_mybatis_sidu project, right-click the src directory and select New – Class. 1-2. Enter com.altibase.sidu.model in the Package field and UserVo in the Name field.

![additional5.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/8.%20Appendix%201%20(MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional5.png?api=v2)

1-3. Write the following content into the UserVo.java file.

```
package com.altibase.sidu.model;

import java.io.Serializable;
import java.util.Date;

@SuppressWarnings("serial")
public class UserVo implements Serializable {
	private Integer userNo;
	private String userName;
	private String userContent;
	private Date regDate;

	public Integer getUserNo() {
		return userNo;
	}

	public void setUserNo(Integer userNo) {
		this.userNo = userNo;
	}

	public String getUserName() {
		return userName;
	}

	public void setUserName(String userName) {
		this.userName = userName;
	}

	public String getUserContent() {
		return userContent;
	}

	public void setUserContent(String userContent) {
		this.userContent = userContent;
	}

	public Date getRegDate() {
		return regDate;
	}

	public void setRegDate(Date regDate) {
		this.regDate = regDate;
	}

	public String toString() {
		return "user_no = " + this.userNo + "\n" + "user_name = "
				+ this.userName + "\n" + "user_content = " + this.userContent
				+ "\n" + "reg_date = " + this.regDate;
	}

}
```

2. Create the MyBatisUtil.java class, which includes the DB connection and necessary methods.

2-1. In the altibase_mybatis_sidu project, right-click the src directory and select New – Class. 2-2. Enter com.altibase.sidu.util in the Package field and MybatisUtil in the Name field.

![additional6.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/8.%20Appendix%201%20(MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional6.png?api=v2)

2-3. Write the following content into the MybatisUtil.java file.

```
package com.altibase.sidu.util;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.InputStream;
import java.text.ParsePosition;
import java.text.SimpleDateFormat;
import java.util.Calendar;

import org.apache.ibatis.io.Resources;
import org.apache.ibatis.session.SqlSession;
import org.apache.ibatis.session.SqlSessionFactory;
import org.apache.ibatis.session.SqlSessionFactoryBuilder;

public class MybatisUtil {

	private static SqlSessionFactory sqlSessionFactory;
	private static SqlSession sqlSession;

	public static SqlSession getSqlSessionFactory() {
		if (sqlSessionFactory == null) {
			InputStream inputStream;
			try {
				inputStream = Resources
						.getResourceAsStream("mybatis-config.xml");
				sqlSessionFactory = new SqlSessionFactoryBuilder()
						.build(inputStream);
				sqlSession = sqlSessionFactory.openSession(false);
			} catch (IOException e) {
				throw new RuntimeException(e.getCause());
			}
		}
		return sqlSession;
	}

	public String NulltoStr(String str) {
		if (str == null) {
			str = "";
		}
		return str;
	}

	public String getFormatDate(String date, String originalformat,
			String wantformat) {
		java.util.Date d = null;
		SimpleDateFormat dd = new SimpleDateFormat(originalformat);
		ParsePosition parse = new ParsePosition(0);
		d = dd.parse(date, parse);
		Calendar cal = Calendar.getInstance();
		cal.setTime(d);
		SimpleDateFormat sdf = new SimpleDateFormat(wantformat);
		String day = sdf.format(cal.getTime());
		return day;
	}
}
```

3. Create a class that obtains a SqlSession object from the MybatisUtil class and executes queries.

In the example, separate classes were declared for each DML operation. This example explains only the Select case.

3.1 In the altibase\_mybatis\_sidu project, right-click the src directory and select New – Class.

3.2 Enter com.altibase.sidu.application in the Package field and SiduSampleSelect in the Name field.

![additional7.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/8.%20Appendix%201%20(MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional7.png?api=v2)

3.3 Write the following content in the SiduSampleSelect.java file.

```
package com.altibase.sidu.application;

import java.sql.SQLException;
import java.util.List;
import com.altibase.sidu.model.UserVo;
import com.altibase.sidu.util.MybatisUtil;

public class SiduSampleSelect {

	public UserVo SiduSelect(int user_no) {
		UserVo userVo = new UserVo();

		try {
			String statement = "com.altibase.sidu.mapper.UserMapper.selectUserData";
			userVo = MybatisUtil.getSqlSessionFactory().selectOne(statement,
					user_no);

			return userVo;
		} catch (Exception e) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException(e);
		}
	}

	public List<UserVo> SiduSelectList() throws SQLException {
		String statement = "com.altibase.sidu.mapper.UserMapper.selectAllUserData";
		List<UserVo> userVos = MybatisUtil.getSqlSessionFactory().selectList(statement);

		return userVos;
	}
}
```

4. Write the Main class, where the actual program runs, in the SiduMain.java file.

```
package com.altibase.sidu.application;

import java.util.Calendar;
import java.util.List;

import com.altibase.sidu.model.UserVo;

public class SiduMain {

	/**
	 * @param args
	 */
	public static void main(String[] args) {

		UserVo userVo = new UserVo();
		int user_no = 1;
		int res_count = 0;

		try {
			// Insert example
			userVo.setUserNo(user_no);
			userVo.setUserName("sidu_1");
			userVo.setUserContent("sidu_content_1");
			userVo.setRegDate(Calendar.getInstance().getTime());
			SiduSampleInsert sidu_insert = new SiduSampleInsert(userVo);
			res_count = sidu_insert.SiduInsert();

			// Select example
			SiduSampleSelect sidu_select = new SiduSampleSelect();
			userVo = sidu_select.SiduSelect(user_no);

			System.out.println(userVo.toString());

			// Insert example
			userVo.setUserNo(5);
			sidu_insert = new SiduSampleInsert(userVo);
			res_count = sidu_insert.SiduInsert();
			System.out.println("insert count = " + res_count);

			// Update example
			userVo.setUserName("sidu_5");
			userVo.setUserContent("sidu_content_5");
			userVo.setRegDate(Calendar.getInstance().getTime());
			SiduSampleUpdate sidu_update = new SiduSampleUpdate(userVo);
			res_count = sidu_update.SiduUpdate();
			System.out.println("update count = " + res_count);

			// Delete example
			user_no = 5;
			SiduSampleDelete sidu_delete = new SiduSampleDelete(user_no);
			res_count = sidu_delete.SiduDelete();
			System.out.println("delete count = " + res_count);

			// Select All example
			List<UserVo> userVos = sidu_select.SiduSelectList();

			for(int i=0; i<userVos.size(); i++) {
				userVo = userVos.get(i);

				System.out.println("object " + (i+1));
				System.out.println(userVo.toString());
			}

			// If the same test is run twice, two rows with user_no=1 can exist and only select may run.
			// Because the program can terminate when SelectOne is used, also delete the row whose user_no is 1.
			user_no = 1;
			sidu_delete = new SiduSampleDelete(user_no);
			res_count = sidu_delete.SiduDelete();

		}
		catch(Exception e) {
			e.getStackTrace();
		}

	}

}
```

# 9. Appendix 2(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase Integration)
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=22643036
Updated: 2025-10-21T09:32:25.000+0900

- [Create DB Tables and Sequences](#id-9.Appendix2(Spring-MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-CreateDBTablesandSequences) - [Spring Installation](#id-9.Appendix2(Spring-MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-SpringInstallation) - [Maven Installation](#id-9.Appendix2(Spring-MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-MavenInstallation) - [Project Creation](#id-9.Appendix2(Spring-MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-ProjectCreation) - [Package Naming Convention](#id-9.Appendix2(Spring-MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-PackageNamingConvention) - [Creating the ApplicationContext File](#id-9.Appendix2(Spring-MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-CreatingtheApplicationContextFile) - [Create the Mapper File](#id-9.Appendix2(Spring-MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-CreatetheMapperFile) - [Dependency Injection](#id-9.Appendix2(Spring-MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-DependencyInjection) - [Application Development](#id-9.Appendix2(Spring-MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-ApplicationDevelopment) - [Creating related JAR files](#id-9.Appendix2(Spring-MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-CreatingrelatedJARfiles) - [Running the Application](#id-9.Appendix2(Spring-MyBatis-AltibaseIntegration)-RunningtheApplication)

Based on the altibase_mybatis_spring example, this appendix provides a more detailed explanation of how to integrate Spring-MyBatis with Altibase. Note that the IDE used is Eclipse.

## Create DB Tables and Sequences

---

Create the following tables and sequences in the database.

```
create table users(
  user_no integer,
  user_name varchar(30),
  user_content varchar(200),
  reg_date date
);
```

## Spring Installation

---

To use Spring, you need to install STS (SpringSource Tools Suite). STS is a plugin for Eclipse that provides convenient tools for developing with Spring within Eclipse. Install the version that matches your Eclipse version from the list below.

![additional2_1.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_1.png?api=v2)

## Maven Installation

---

- Maven is a software project management tool developed by the Apache Software Foundation. Based on the Project Object Model (POM), Maven manages the entire project lifecycle including build, test, and documentation. The Spring-MyBatis-Altibase integration test source is also managed using Maven. This section explains the Maven installation process.

    1. Download Maven Files Download the binary zip file from [http://maven.apache.org/download.html](http://maven.apache.org/download.html). (As of October 2014, the latest version is apache-maven-3.2.8-bin.zip.)
    2. Configure Maven Environment After extracting the files, add MAVEN_HOME (e.g., c:\maven) to the user variables in Windows Environment Variables (Desktop -> My Computer -> Properties -> Advanced -> Environment Variables).

![additional2_2.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_2.png?api=v2)

Include the Maven binary path in the PATH environment variable.

![additional2_3.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_3.png?api=v2)

- In Windows, go to Start → Run → type `cmd` to open the command prompt. Then, enter `mvn –version`. If the version information appears, the setup is successful.

![additional2_4.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_4.png?api=v2)

3. Download Maven in Eclipse

- In Eclipse, go to Help → Eclipse Marketplace, and download Maven just like you do when downloading STS.

![additional2_5.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_5.png?api=v2)

4. Set the extracted Maven in Eclipse.

Go to Windows → Preferences → Maven → Installations, click Browse, and select the path to “C:\maven\conf\settings.xml”, then click Apply.

![additional2_6.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_6.png?api=v2)

## Project Creation

---

After installing STS in Eclipse, you can create Spring-based projects using Spring Template Project. Follow the steps below to create a project:

1. From the menu, click File → New → Spring Template Project, and create a Spring MVC Project.

![additional2_7.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_7.png?api=v2)

2. For Project name: enter: `altibase_mybatis_spring`, for Top-level package, enter: `com.altibase.test` (Spring requires a default package name when creating a project.)

![additional2_8.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_8.png?api=v2)

3. Click the Finish button.

## Package Naming Convention

---

The package name used in this example is based on a common naming convention and follows the structure `com.altibase.test`, as explained in the appendix. Each part of the package name has a specific meaning:

- **com**: The first part indicates the nature of the organization leading the project. “com” stands for “company.” For smaller groups or non-commercial organizations, “org” (organization) is often used.
- **altibase**: The second part represents the name of the company or organization. Since this document is created by Altibase, it uses "altibase."
- **test**: The third part reflects the specific artifact or purpose of the project. In this case, the project demonstrates general DML operations (Select/Insert/Delete/Update), so "test" is used.

## Creating the ApplicationContext File

---

In Spring development, the first thing you should do is create the **ApplicationContext** file, which is the Spring bean configuration file. The following section describes the contents of this configuration file.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<beans xmlns="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans"
	xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
	xmlns:context="http://www.springframework.org/schema/context"
	xmlns:tx="http://www.springframework.org/schema/tx"
	xmlns:p="http://www.springframework.org/schema/p"
	xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans/spring-beans-3.0.xsd
		http://www.springframework.org/schema/tx http://www.springframework.org/schema/tx/spring-tx-3.1.xsd
		http://www.springframework.org/schema/context http://www.springframework.org/schema/context/spring-context-3.0.xsd">

	<description>Example configuration to get you started.</description>

	<!-- Search for beans in the specified package -->
	<context:component-scan base-package="com.altibase.test.service" />

	 <!-- How to connect to ALTIBASE DB using Apache DBCP.
	      Apache DBCP provides properties for initializing the session pool, and it can create initialSize sessions on the first connection. -->
	<bean id="dataSource" class="org.apache.commons.dbcp.BasicDataSource" destroy-method="close">
        <property name="driverClassName" value="Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver" />
        <property name="url" value="jdbc:Altibase://192.168.1.62:21020/mydb" />
        <property name="username" value="test" />
        <property name="password" value="test" />
        <property name="initialSize" value="10" />
        <property name="minIdle" value="25" />
        <property name="maxIdle" value="30" />
        <property name="maxActive" value="100" />
        <property name="validationQuery" value="select 1 from dual" />
        <property name="testOnBorrow" value="false" />
    </bean>

	<!-- Enable transactions -->
	<bean id="txManager" class="org.springframework.jdbc.datasource.DataSourceTransactionManager">
		<property name="dataSource" ref="dataSource" />
	</bean>

	<!-- Define transaction annotations -->
	<tx:annotation-driven transaction-manager="txManager"/>

	<!-- Define SqlSessionFactory -->
	<!-- In the typeAliasesPackage property, specify the package containing domain classes referenced by SQL statements in mapper definition files (XML). -->
	<bean id="sqlSessionFactory" class="org.mybatis.spring.SqlSessionFactoryBean">
		<property name="dataSource" ref="dataSource" />
		<property name="typeAliasesPackage" value="com.altibase.test.domain" />
	</bean>

	<!-- Allow mapper classes created from mapper interfaces and mapper definition files to be injected into beans. -->
	<bean class="org.mybatis.spring.mapper.MapperScannerConfigurer">
		<property name="basePackage" value="com.altibase.test.persistence" />
	</bean>
</beans>
```

## Create the Mapper File

---

Create a Mapper file that defines the CRUD SQL statements for the Users table and the corresponding mapping methods. Since it follows the Spring approach, Dependency Injection is used. (UserMapper.xml, UserMapper.java) The Mapper will be created in the `com.altibase.test.persistence` package.

1. In the `altibase_mybatis_spring` project, right-click the `src` directory, then click New → Package to create a new package named `com.altibase.test.persistence`.

![additional2_9.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_9.png?api=v2)

2. Right-click the newly created package (com.altibase.test.persistence), select New - Interface, and create the UserMapper.java file.
3. Write the contents of the created interface file as follows.

```
package com.altibase.test.persistence;

import java.util.List;

import com.altibase.test.domain.UserVo;

public interface UserMapper {
	public List<UserVo> getAllUser();
	public UserVo getUserByNo(int user_no);
	public Integer insertUserData(UserVo userVo);
	public Integer deleteUserByNo(int user_no);
	public Integer updateUserByNo(UserVo userVo);

}
```

4. Right-click the newly created package (com.altibase.test.persistence), select New - File, and enter UserMapper.xml in File name.

![additional2_10.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_10.png?api=v2)

5. Write the following content in UserMapper.xml.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE mapper PUBLIC "-//mybatis.org//DTD Mapper 3.0//EN"
"http://mybatis.org/dtd/mybatis-3-mapper.dtd">

<mapper namespace="com.altibase.test.persistence.UserMapper">
	<select id="getAllUser" parameterType="Integer" resultType="UserVo">
		SELECT user_no as userNo,
		user_name as userName,
		user_content as userContent,
		reg_date as regDate
		FROM users
		WHERE user_no = #{userNo}
	</select>

	<select id="getUserByNo"  resultType="UserVo">
		SELECT user_no as userNo,
		user_name as userName,
		user_content as userContent,
		reg_date as regDate
		FROM users
	</select>

	<insert id="insertUserData" parameterType="UserVo">
		insert into
		users(user_no, user_name, user_content, reg_date)
		values(#{userNo}, #{userName}, #{userContent}, #{regDate})
	</insert>

	<update id="updateUserByNo" parameterType="UserVo">
		update users
		set user_name = #{userName},
		user_content = #{userContent},
		reg_date = #{regDate}
		where user_no = #{userNo}
	</update>

	<delete id="deleteUserByNo" parameterType="Integer">
		delete from users
		where user_no = #{userNo}
	</delete>
</mapper>
```

This method is specific to Spring and uses Dependency Injection (DI). In the application, SQL statements are handled through methods defined in the interface.

## Dependency Injection

---

Dependency Injection (abbreviated as DI) literally means injecting dependencies.

Dependency Injection is a technique from the GoF design patterns where the methods to be used by the user are defined in an interface and separated from the actual logic implementation.

With this approach, users can work with only the methods of the interface, and the actual implementation is injected later. This supports clearer separation of work and makes it easy to switch implementation classes.

## Application Development

---

1. Create the UserVo class (UserVo.java), a value object (VO) for the users table.
1-1. In the src/main/java directory of the altibase_mybatis_spring project, right-click and select New - Class.
1-2. Enter com.altibase.test.domain for Package and UserVo for Name.

![additional2_11.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_11.png?api=v2)

1-3. Write the following content in the UserVo.java file.

```
package com.altibase.test.domain;

import java.io.Serializable;
import java.util.Date;

@SuppressWarnings("serial")
public class UserVo implements Serializable {
	private Integer userNo;
	private String userName;
	private String userContent;
	private Date regDate;

	public UserVo() {

	}

	public UserVo(Integer userNo, String userName, String userContent, Date regDate) {
		this.userNo = userNo;
		this.userName = userName;
		this.userContent = userContent;
		this.regDate = regDate;
	}

	public Integer getUserNo() {
		return userNo;
	}

	public void setUserNo(Integer userNo) {
		this.userNo = userNo;
	}

	public String getUserName() {
		return userName;
	}

	public void setUserName(String userName) {
		this.userName = userName;
	}

	public String getUserContent() {
		return userContent;
	}

	public void setUserContent(String userContent) {
		this.userContent = userContent;
	}

	public Date getRegDate() {
		return regDate;
	}

	public void setRegDate(Date regDate) {
		this.regDate = regDate;
	}

	@Override
	public String toString() {
		return "User [no=" + userNo + ", name=" + userName + ", content=" + userContent
				+ ", date=" + regDate + "]";
	}
}
```

2. Create the interface and injection class files that execute the actual queries.
2-1. In the src/main/java directory of the altibase_mybatis_spring project, right-click and select New - Interface.
2-2. Enter com.altibase.test.service for Package and UserService for Name.

![additional2_12.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_12.png?api=v2)

2-3. Write the following content in the UserService.java file.

```
package com.altibase.test.service;

import java.util.List;
import com.altibase.test.domain.UserVo;

public interface UserService {
	public List<UserVo> getAllUser();
	public UserVo getUserByNo(int user_no);
	public Integer insertUserData(UserVo userVo);
	public Integer deleteUserByNo(int user_no);
	public Integer updateUserByNo(UserVo userVo);
}
```

2-4. Right-click the newly created package (com.altibase.test.service), then click New - Class to create the UserServiceImpl.java class file that handles the actual logic.

![additional2_13.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_13.png?api=v2)

2-5. Write the following content in the UserServiceImpl.java file.

```
package com.altibase.test.service;

import java.util.List;

import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

import com.altibase.test.domain.UserVo;
import com.altibase.test.persistence.UserMapper;

@Service("userService")
public class UserServiceImpl implements UserService {

	@Autowired
	private UserMapper userMapper;
	private Integer res_count;

	public List<UserVo> getAllUser() {
		List<UserVo> userVos = userMapper.getAllUser();
		return userVos;
	}

	public UserVo getUserByNo(int user_no) {
		UserVo userVo = userMapper.getUserByNo(user_no);
		return userVo;
	}

	public Integer insertUserData(UserVo userVo) {
		res_count = userMapper.insertUserData(userVo);
		return res_count;
	}

	public Integer deleteUserByNo(int user_no) {
		res_count = userMapper.deleteUserByNo(user_no);
		return res_count;
	}

	public Integer updateUserByNo(UserVo userVo) {
		res_count = userMapper.updateUserByNo(userVo);
		return res_count;
	}
}
```

3. Write the Main class, where the actual program runs, in the Main.java file.

```
package com.altibase.test;

import java.util.Calendar;

import org.springframework.context.ApplicationContext;
import org.springframework.context.support.ClassPathXmlApplicationContext;

import com.altibase.test.domain.UserVo;
import com.altibase.test.service.UserService;

public class Main {

	private static UserService userService;

	public static void main(String[] args) {
		// TODO Auto-generated method stub
		int res_count = 0;

		ApplicationContext applicationContext = new ClassPathXmlApplicationContext("META-INF/spring/ApplicationContext.xml");
		userService = (UserService)applicationContext.getBean("userService");

		UserVo userVo = new UserVo();

		// Insert sample
		userVo.setUserNo(1);
		userVo.setUserName("psy");
		userVo.setUserContent("psy_content");
		userVo.setRegDate(Calendar.getInstance().getTime());
		res_count = userService.insertUserData(userVo);
		System.out.println("insert count = " + res_count);

		// Select sample
		userVo = userService.getUserByNo(1);
		System.out.println("no = " + userVo.getUserNo());
		System.out.println("name = " + userVo.getUserName());
		System.out.println("content = " + userVo.getUserContent());
		System.out.println("date = " + userVo.getRegDate());

		// Update sample
		userVo.setUserName("updated_psy");
		userVo.setUserContent("updated_psy_content");
		res_count = userService.updateUserByNo(userVo);
		System.out.println("update count = " + res_count);

		// Delete sample
		res_count = userService.deleteUserByNo(userVo.getUserNo());
		System.out.println("delete count = " + res_count);
	}
}
```

## Creating related JAR files

---

There are two ways to add JARs:

- Adding libraries via Maven
- Adding libraries the traditional way (Add External JARs in properties - Java Build Path)

The sample source is written choosing the Maven library management method. Since the second method, the traditional way, has already been explained above, this chapter will explain the Maven library management method. When you install Maven and create a Spring Template Project, a file called pom.xml is generated. This file manages the libraries.

![additional2_14.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_14.png?api=v2)

There are two ways to add libraries in the pom.xml file:

- Add libraries by directly entering tags in the pom.xml tab
- Add libraries using the Add button in the Dependencies tab

The method of directly entering tags involves clicking the pom.xml tab to open the XML file and adding the library by typing the tags manually, as shown in the image below. (The library used for testing is the Apache Commons DBCP library.)

![additional2_15.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_15.png?api=v2)

After adding the dependency and saving the XML file, verify that the library has been added to Maven Dependencies.

![additional2_16.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_16.png?api=v2)

To add a library using the Add button in the Dependencies tab, follow these steps:

1) In the pom.xml file, click the dependencies-Add button, which opens the following window. In the field labeled "Enter groupId, artifactId or sha1 prefix or pattern (star):", type the name of the library you want to add, and it will display libraries matching the entered name as shown below.

![additional2_17.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_17.png?api=v2)

2) When you click on a library shown in the Search Results, the available versions for that library will appear. Select the desired version and then click the OK button to add the library.

![additional2_18.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_18.png?api=v2)

You can verify that the library has been successfully added.

![additional2_19.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_19.png?api=v2)

When you save the file, the changes are applied, and the library is added.

![additional2_20.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_20.png?api=v2)

At the end, you can see that not only commons-dbcp but also commons-pool was added. When you add libraries through the dependencies tab, related libraries like these are also added automatically.

## Running the Application

---

Run the altibase_mybatis_spring project. You can either right-click the altibase_mybatis_spring project and select Run from the menu, or open the Main.java class in the com.altibase.test package by double-clicking it and then run it.

![additional2_21.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/9.%20Appendix%202(Spring-MyBatis-Altibase%20Integration)/additional2_21.png?api=v2)

# 1. What is Spring?
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=14058412
Updated: 2025-09-23T10:11:38.000+0900

- [Features of Spring](#id-1.WhatisSpring?-FeaturesofSpring)

The Spring Framework is an open-source application framework and inversion of control container for the Java platform. The framework's core features can be used by any Java application, but there are extensions for building web applications on top of the Java EE (Enterprise Edition) platform. This is a lightweight container compared to EJB container, and manages the lifecycle of plain old Java objects (POJOs), and provides modules such as transaction management, logging, and security.

# **Features of Spring**

---

1. It is a lightweight container compared to J2EE.
2. It manages the life-cycle such as the creation and removal of Java objects, and the program can import and use the required objects from Spring without creating objects.
3. It supports IoC(Inversion of Control) and DI(Dependency Injection). That is, it can set the dependency of objects with the bean configuration file.
4. As it supports AOP (Aspect Oriented Programming), it is commonly used in many modules, but it can be applied to each module by separating functions (eg, functions such as transaction, logging, and security) that are not the core of the actual module.
5. It supports POJO, a general Java object that does not implement a specific interface or inherit a specific class like EJB. Therefore, it can be used in Spring without modifying the existing sources.
6. It provides a consistent method for transaction processing.
7. It provides various APIs.
<!-- SOURCE_BLOCK_END source_id="AID-SRC-000384" block_id="BLOCK-000376" -->

# 2. Setting before Developing Spring
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/2.+Setting+before+Developing+Spring
Updated: 2025-09-23T10:13:52.000+0900

- [Building environment for Spring Framework](#id-2.SettingbeforeDevelopingSpring-BuildingenvironmentforSpringFramework) - [How to get ALTIBASE JDBC Driver](#id-2.SettingbeforeDevelopingSpring-HowtogetALTIBASEJDBCDriver)

In order to use the Spring Framework, jar files related to Spring are required. In addition, in order to integrate with Altibase, the ALTIBASE JDBC Driver is required. This chapter describes how to build an environment for Spring, and how to get an ALTIBASE JDBC Driver.

## **Building environment for Spring Framework**

The environment for Spring can be easily built by using the Eclipse Spring Development Tool (STS) and Maven.

**What is Maven?**

This is a project management tool.

This is a management tool that includes logic for executing plug-in goals in the steps defined in the project object model, standard set, project lifecycle, and dependency management system.

Example of Maven

```
Maven
<dependencies>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>org.springframework</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-context</artifactId>
        <version>3.2.xx.RELEASE</version>
    </dependency>
</dependencies>
```

Information

- Please refer to Appendix 2 of "MyBatis Integration Guide for Altibase"
- The red mark should be set according to the patch version.

## **How to get ALTIBASE JDBC Driver**

The JDBC driver provided by ALTIBASE is Altibase.jar file. This file is located in the $ALTIBASE_HOME/lib directory of the server where ALTIBASE is installed.

Starting from Altibase version 5, Altibase.jar and Altibase5.jar files exist in the $ALTIBASE_HOME/lib directory. Altibase.jar is a general JDBC Driver file, and Altibase5.jar is the JDBC Driver file used when the user wants to integrate ALTIBASE version 5 or lower versions together. Therefore, when integrating with one ALTIBASE DB or multiple ALTIBASEs with the same version, use the $ALTIBASE_HOME/lib/Altibase.jar file.

It is necessary to check the version of ALTIBASE JDBC Driver to verify that the ALTIBASE DB Server to be integrated with the ALTIBASE JDBC Driver is compatible.

To check the ALTIBASE JDBC Driver version, execute the following command.

```
$ java –jar Altibase.jar
JDBC Driver Info : Altibase Ver = 6.3.1.2.6 for JavaVM v1.4, CMP:7.1.1, Oct  6 2014 13:54:56
```

At this time, if the cm protocol version of the ALTIBASE DB Server and the CMP of the ALTIBASE JDBC Driver is the same, they are compatible.

```
$ altibase -v
version 6.3.1.2.7 X86_64_LINUX_redhat_Enterprise_ES4-64bit-6.3.1.2.7-release-GCC3.4.6
(x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) Oct  8 2014 09:16:24, binary db version 6.2.1, meta version 6.3.1,
cm protocol version 7.1.1, replication protocol version 7.4.1
```

It is recommended that the user uses the ALTIBASE JDBC Driver file, which is the same as or later than the version of ALTIBASE DB Server, because JDBC related bugs may be fixed as the version is upgraded.
<!-- SOURCE_BLOCK_END source_id="AID-SRC-000385" block_id="BLOCK-000377" -->

# 3. Setting up JDBC Driver
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/3.+Setting+up+JDBC+Driver
Updated: 2025-09-23T10:14:11.000+0900

- [How to set up in the project (Eclipse)](#id-3.SettingupJDBCDriver-Howtosetupintheproject(Eclipse)) - [How to set up in the web application](#id-3.SettingupJDBCDriver-Howtosetupinthewebapplication)

This chapter describes how to set the ALTIBASE JDBC Driver.

## **How to set up in the project (Eclipse)**

How to add ALTIBASE JDBC Driver to the project in the Eclipse is as follows.

Project - JRE System Library - Properties - Installed JREs - Click jre among the items - Edit - Click Add External JARs and add the ALTIBASE JDBC Driver Altibase.jar.

![datasource_1.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20Setting%20up%20JDBC%20Driver/datasource_1.png?api=v2)

![datasource_2.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20Setting%20up%20JDBC%20Driver/datasource_2.png?api=v2)

## **How to set up in the web application**

If the web application is implemented, the ALTIBASE JDBC Driver can be set in two methods.

The first method is to place the Altibase.jar file in the appropriate directory of each web server, so that all web applications can use the ALTIBASE JDBC Driver globally. This method can be used (refer to the integration guide for each web server).

Another method is to set up the ALTIBASE JDBC Driver only in the web application. If the ALTIBASE JDBC Driver is used in the web application, Altibase.jar can be placed in the following location.

|  |
| --- |
| `Web_application\WEB-INF\lib` |

If the project is created with Eclipse as Web Project, Altibase.jar is located in the following directory.

|  |
| --- |
| `project\WebContent\WEB-INF\lib` |

![datasource_3.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20Setting%20up%20JDBC%20Driver/datasource_3.png?api=v2)
<!-- SOURCE_BLOCK_END source_id="AID-SRC-000386" block_id="BLOCK-000378" -->

# 4. Configuring DataSource
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/4.+Configuring+DataSource
Updated: 2025-09-23T10:14:26.000+0900

- [Using DriverManagerDataSource](#id-4.ConfiguringDataSource-UsingDriverManagerDataSource) - [Using DBCP](#id-4.ConfiguringDataSource-UsingDBCP) - [Using the ConnectionPool of ALTIBASE](#id-4.ConfiguringDataSource-UsingtheConnectionPoolofALTIBASE)

In order to integrate with DB in Spring, DataSource related bean must be configured in the bean configuration file.

(In this document, the name of the bean configuration file was defined as applicationContext.xml.)

There is the method of using the DriverManagerDataSource provided by the Spring Framework, the method of using the DBCP provided by Jakarta, and the method of using the ConnectionPool provided by the DB vendor. This chapter describes how to integrate with Altibase using these methods.

## **Using DriverManagerDataSource**

In the case of integrating with DB using DriverManagerDataSource class provided by Spring Framework, set class property value as org.springframework.jdbc.datasource.DriverManagerDataSource when setting dataSource bean in the bean configuration file.

At this time, various properties for integrating with DB can be defined in the dataSource bean. The following properties can be defined according to ALTIBASE.

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| driverClassName | ALTIBASE JDBC driver class name |
| URL | Connection string information for connecting with ALTIBASE in the form of "jdbc:Altibase://IP:port_no/db_name" |
| username | Database account |
| password | Database password |

The following is part of the applicationContext.xml file of DataManagerDataSourceConnection provided as an example. Ex) applicationContext.xml file of DataManagerDataSourceConnection.

```
…
<bean id="dataSource"
    class="org.springframework.jdbc.datasource.DriverManagerDataSource">
    <!-- JDBC Driver class name setting -->
    <property name="driverClassName" value="Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver" />
    <      <!-- connection url -->
    <property name="url" value="jdbc:Altibase://192.168.1.35:21129/mydb" />
    <!-- DB user account settings -->
    <property name="username" value="sys" />
    <!-- DB user password setting -->
    <property name="password" value="manager" />
</bean>
…
```

To run the DataManagerDataSourceConnection project included in the example, Altibase.jar, spring.jar, spring-jdbc.jar, and common-logging.jar files are needed, so the corresponding jar files must be added.

![datasource_4.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/4.%20Configuring%20DataSource/datasource_4.png?api=v2)

## **Using DBCP**

ConnectionPool based DataSource can be configured using DBCP (Jakarta Commons Database Connection Pool) API provided by Jakarta in the Spring. The DataSource class used at this time is org.apache.commons.dbcp.BasicDataSource. To set it up, use the BasicDataSource class in the applicationContext.xml file as in the DriverManagerDataSource class described above, and create a dataSource bean.

Ex) applicationContext.xml file of DBCPConnection

```
…
<bean id="dataSource" class="org.apache.commons.dbcp.BasicDataSource">
    <!-- JDBC Driver class name setting -->
    <property name="driverClassName" value="Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver" />
    <!-- connection url -->
    <property name="url" value="jdbc:Altibase://192.168.1.35:21129/mydb" />
    <!-- DB user account setting -->
    <property name="username" value="sys" />
    <!-- DB user password setting -->
    <property name="password" value="manager" />
</bean>
…
```

BasicDataSource class provides various properties to manage ConnectionPool.

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| driverClassName | ALTIBASE JDBC driver class name |
| url | Connection string information for connecting with ALTIBASE in the form of `jdbc:Altibase://IP:port_no/db_name` |
| username | Database account |
| password | Database password |
| maxActive | The maximum number of connections. 0 is unlimited. The default is 8. |
| initialSize | The initial number of connections. The default is 0. |
| maxIdle | The maximum number of connections that remain idle in the pool. The default is 8. |
| maxWait | The maximum connection attempt time (unit: millisec) -1 waits infinitely. The default is infinite waiting. |
| validationQuery | SQL statement used to check connection validation Must be specified as a select statement that returns at least one row. ex) select 1 from dual |
| defaultAutoCommit | Set autocommit mode. The default is true. |
| defaultTransactionIsolation | Set Transaction Isolation level The values of NONE, REPEATABLE_READ, and SERIALIZABLE can be set, and the default follows the default value of the DB server. The isolation level of ALTIBASE is READ COMMITTED by default. |

To run the DBCPConnection project included in the example, in addition to the Spring configuration library file, the Altibase.jar, common-logging.jar, common-dbcp.jar, and common-pools.jar files are required.

![datasource_5.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/4.%20Configuring%20DataSource/datasource_5.png?api=v2)

## **Using the ConnectionPool of ALTIBASE**

If the user uses the AltibaseConnectionPoolDataSource class provided by ALTIBASE, the user can use the ConnectionPool of ALTIBASE. Like other DataSource described previously, the user can define dataSource bean by using the AltibaseConnectionPoolDataSource class in applicationContext.xml.

Ex) applicationContext.xml file of AltibaseConnectionPool

```
…
<bean id="dataSource"
class="Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseConnectionPoolDataSource">
  <!-- Connection URL uppercase note -->
  <property name="URL" value="jdbc:Altibase://192.168.1.35:21129/mydb"/>
  <!-- DB user account setting -->
  <property name="user" value="sys"/>
  <!-- DB user password setting -->
<property name="password" value="manager" />
</bean>
…
```

When using AltibaseConnectionPoolDataSource, the ALTIBASE JDBC Driver class is automatically loaded from AltibaseConnectionPoolDataSource, so there is no need to specify the driverClassName property. In addition, note that the property representing the DB user account is user, not username.

AltibaseConnectionPoolDataSource class provides various properties to manage the ConnectionPool.

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| URL | Connection string information for connecting with ALTIBASE in the form of `jdbc:Altibase://IP:port_no/db_name` |
| user | Database account |
| password | Database password |
| maxPoolSize | The maximum number of connections. The default is 10. |
| minPoolSize | The minimum number of connections. The default is 0. |
| initialPoolSize | The initial number of connections. The default is 1. |
| maxIdleTime | The idle waiting time |
| propertyCycle | The wait time when ConnectionPool is full (millisec) |

To run AltibaseConnectionPool project included in the example, Altibase.jar, spring.jar, spring-jdbc.jar, and common-logging.jar files are required.

![datasource_6.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/4.%20Configuring%20DataSource/datasource_6.png?api=v2)
<!-- SOURCE_BLOCK_END source_id="AID-SRC-000387" block_id="BLOCK-000379" -->

# 5. Additional Connection
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/5.+Additional+Connection
Updated: 2025-09-23T10:14:41.000+0900

- [Connection using FailOver](#id-5.AdditionalConnection-ConnectionusingFailOver) - [Simultaneously connecting ALTIBASE and the previous version](#id-5.AdditionalConnection-SimultaneouslyconnectingALTIBASEandthepreviousversion)

This chapter describes how to integrate FailOver and Altibase Multi-version provided by Altibase.

## **Connection using FailOver**

FailOver is supported starting from ALTIBASE 5.3.3. To use FailOver, FailOver-related properties must be placed in the Connection URL section.

The following is an example of connecting to ALTIBASE using the FailOver. DataSource used DBCP among the methods described above.

Ex) applicationContext.xml file of FailOverConnection

```
…
<bean id="dataSource" class="org.apache.commons.dbcp.BasicDataSource">
<!-- JDBC Driver class name setting -->
<property name="driverClassName" value="Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver" />
<property name="URL"
  value="jdbc:Altibase://192.168.1.62:21020/mydb?AlternateServers=(192.168.1.146:21020)
&ConnectionRetryCount=1&ConnectionRetryDelay=1&SessionFailOver=off
&LoadBalance=off”/>
" />
<property name="username" value="test" />
<property name="password" value="test" />
</bean>
…
```

FailOver related properties that can be defined in the Connection URL section are as follows.

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| AlternateServer | Alternative servers to be connected in the event of a failure (IP Address1:Port1, IP Address2:Port2,...) |
| ConnectionRetryCount | The number of retries of connection attempts when an available server connection fails |
| ConnectionRetryDelay | The time to wait before attempting to connect again when the available server connection fails (in seconds) |
| LoadBalance | If set to on, random selection is made including the default server and available servers when the first connection is attempted. If set to off, it connects to the default server when it tries to connect for the first time, and if it fails, it connects to the server described by AlternateServer. |
| SessionFailOver | This indicates whether to perform STF (Service Time Fail-Over). on: STF, off: CTF<br>CTF(Connection Time Fail-Over) recognizes a failure at DBMS connection time, connects to another available node's DBMS instead of the failed DBMS, and proceeds with service.<br>STF(Service Time Fail-Over) means a failure occurs during service after DBMS connection succeeds; it reconnects to another available node's DBMS, restores session properties, and lets the user application perform its business logic again. This applies when the operation performed on the failed DBMS must be performed once more. |

Please refer to the FailOverConnection project among the attached examples.

To run the FailOverConnection project, Altibase.jar, spring-jdbc.jar, and common-logging.jar files are required in addition to the Spring configuration library file.

## **Simultaneously connecting ALTIBASE and the previous version**

ALTIBASE can connect to lower versions simultaneously in one application.

In order to distinguish it from the existing Altibase.jar, the ALTIBASE version 5 of JDBC Altibase5.jar, which has been renamed separately, is required.

The following is an example of loading the drivers of two versions of ALTIBASE by using Altibase.jar and Altibase5.jar files.

Ex) applicationContext.xml file of MultiVersionConnection

```
<!— DataSource setting for ALTIBASE version 6 -->
<bean id="dataSource1" class="org.springframework.jdbc.datasource.DriverManagerDataSource">
<!--  JDBC Driver class name setting -->
   <property name="driverClassName" value="Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver"/>
   <!-- Connection URL uppercase note -->
   <property name="URL" value="jdbc:Altibase://127.0.0.1:20300/mydb"/>
   <!-- DB user account setting -->
   <property name="username" value="sys"/>
   <!-- DB user password setting -->
<property name="password" value="manager" />
</bean>

<!—DataSource setting for versions earlier than ALTIBASE 6 -->
<bean id="dataSource2" class="org.springframework.jdbc.datasource.DriverManagerDataSource">
<!--  JDBC Driver class name setting -->
<property name="driverClassName" value="Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver"/>
   <!-- Connection URL uppercase note -->
   <property name="URL" value="jdbc:Altibase://192.168.1.35:21129/mydb"/>
   <!-- DB user account setting -->
   <property name="username" value="sys"/>
   <!-- DB user password setting -->
   <property name="password" value="manager" />
</bean>

<!-- bean setting of DAO class -->
<bean id="accountDao1" class="com.altibase.banking.AccountDao">
   <property name="dataSource" ref="dataSource1"/>
</bean>

<!-- bean setting of DAO class -->
<bean id="accountDao2" class="com.altibase.banking.AccountDao">
   <property name="dataSource" ref="dataSource2"/>
</bean>
…
```

AccountApp.java file of MultiVersionConnection

```
…
Resource resource = new ClassPathResource("applicationContext.xml");
BeanFactory factory = new XmlBeanFactory(resource);

AccountDao accountDao1 = (AccountDao)factory.getBean("accountDao1");
AccountDao accountDao2 = (AccountDao)factory.getBean("accountDao2");
…
```

To run the MultiVersionConnection project included in the example, Altibase.jar and Altibase5.jar files are required as well as the existing jar files. These files are located in the lib directory where ALTIBASE is installed ($ALTIBASE_HOME). Use the Altibase5.jar file for ALTIBASE version 5 and the Altibase.jar file for previous versions.

![additional_conn_1.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/5.%20Additional%20Connection/additional_conn_1.png?api=v2)

# 6. Transaction Manager
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/6.+Transaction+Manager
Updated: 2025-09-23T10:14:53.000+0900

- [DataSourceTransactionManager Configuration](#id-6.TransactionManager-DataSourceTransactionManagerConfiguration) - [Declarative transaction processing using TransactionProxyFactoryBean](#id-6.TransactionManager-DeclarativetransactionprocessingusingTransactionProxyFactoryBean) - [Distributed Transaction Process](#id-6.TransactionManager-DistributedTransactionProcess)

Using the Spring Framework, there are various ways to process transactions. First, specify the transaction manager in the bean configuration file and process the transaction. Transaction processing can be implemented directly in the source as needed, or declaratively in the bean configuration file.

Spring Framework provides implementation classes of PlatformTransactionManager interfaces according to the database integrating technology. These classes can be specified as TransactionManager. For example, the DataSourceTransactionManager class can be specified as TransactionManager to process local transactions, and the JtaTransactionManager class can be specified as TransactionManager to process distributed transactions.

In order to declaratively process the transaction after specifying the TransactionManager, define the bean that processes the transaction in the bean configuration file. At this time, specify the TransactionProxyFactoryBean class for this bean to specify how to process the transaction for each method name.

This chapter describes how to set these classes as TransactionManager and how to process transactions declaratively using bean files.

## **DataSourceTransactionManager Configuration**

Among the PlatformTransactionManager implementation classes, TransactionManager can be specified by using the DataSourceTransactionManager class. Simply specify org.springframework.jdbc.datasource.DataSourceTransactionManager class in transactionManager bean in the bean configuration file (applicationContext.xml). Then, when processing the transaction declaratively, specify the transactionManager bean defined for the transaction properties among the properties of the bean that processes the transaction.

Ex) applicationContext.xml file of DataSourceTransactionManager

```
…
<bean id="transactionManager"
class="org.springframework.jdbc.datasource.DataSourceTransactionManager">
   <property name="dataSource" ref="dataSource"/>
</bean>

<bean id="txProxyTemplate" abstract="true"
class="org.springframework.transaction.interceptor.TransactionProxyFactoryBean">
    <property name="transactionManager"  ref="transactionManager" />
    <property name="transactionAttributes">
       <props>
      <prop key="get*">PROPAGATION_REQUIRED, readOnly </prop>
      <prop key="add*">PROPAGATION_REQUIRED</prop>
       </props>
    </property>
</bean>

<bean id="accountService" parent="txProxyTemplate">
<property name="target">
        <bean class="com.altibase.banking.AccountService">
            <property name="accountDao" ref="accountDao"/>
        </bean>
    </property>
</bean>
…
```

In order to process the transaction, the user needs to know how to manage the transaction (TransactionManager) and how to process the transaction. The above example uses the springframework.transaction.interceptor.TransactionProxyFactoryBean class among the transaction processing methods to configure the bean configuration file (applicationContext.xml) as a method to process transactions declaratively (the details are described below).

## **Declarative transaction processing using TransactionProxyFactoryBean**

TransactionProxyFactoryBean class is a class that provides various properties to process transactions. The bean of TransactionProxyFactoryBean class can be set in the bean configuration file (applicationContext.xml), and defines the method of handling the transaction each method to process transactions declaratively. Transaction related properties specified in <property> of bean for processing this transaction are as follows.

1. target
  Sets the object to which the transaction applies with properties
2. transactionManager
  Sets the TransactionManager defined above
3. transactionAttributes
  Sets the properties object used when setting transaction properties. At this time, the transaction property is defined by using the <prop> tag in the unit of the method to which the transaction is applied

The tag value of <prop> is specified in the following format.

```
PROPAGATION, ISOLATION_NAME, readOnly, timeout, +Exception, -Exception
```

Description of each item of <prop> tag value is as follows

|  | Description |
| --- | --- |
| PROPAGATION | Specify transaction propagation rules. Required. PROPAGATION_REQUIRED(Default value), PROPAGATION_REQUIRES_NEW, PROPAGATION_MANDATORY, PROPAGATION_SUPPORTS, PROPAGATION_NOT_SUPPORTED, PROPAGATION_NEVER, PROPAGATION_NESTED |
| ISOLATION_NAME | Set ISOLATION property. Optional. DEFAULT, READ_COMMITTED, READ_UNCOMMITTED, REPETABLE_READ, SERIALIZABLE.<br>ALTIBASE only supports READ_COMMITTED, SERIALIZABLE, and REPETABLE_READ. |
| readOnly | Set transaction read-only when readOnly is used. |
| timeout | Set the transaction timeout time in seconds |
| +,-Exception | Set ROLLBACK rule. +Exception executes COMMIT even if the corresponding Exception occurs, and --Exception performs ROLLBACK when the corresponding Exception occurs. |

The following is a bean configuration file (applicationContext.xml) that defines transaction properties by using the TransactionProxyFactoryBean class.

Ex) applicationContext.xml file of DataSourceTransactionManager

```
…
<bean id="transactionManager"
class="org.springframework.jdbc.datasource.DataSourceTransactionManager">
   <property name="dataSource" ref="dataSource"/>
</bean>

<bean id="txProxyTemplate" abstract="true"
class="org.springframework.transaction.interceptor.TransactionProxyFactoryBean">
    <property name="transactionManager"  ref="transactionManager" />
    <property name="transactionAttributes">
       <props>
      <prop key="get*">PROPAGATION_REQUIRED, readOnly </prop>
      <prop key="add*">PROPAGATION_REQUIRED</prop>
       </props>
    </property>
</bean>

<bean id="accountService" parent="txProxyTemplate">
<property name="target">
        <bean class="com.altibase.banking.AccountService">
            <property name="accountDao" ref="accountDao"/>
        </bean>
    </property>
</bean>

…
```

## **Distributed Transaction Process**

In Spring, JOTM (Java Open Transaction Manager) can be used to process distributed transactions. At this time, in order to integrate with JOTM, JotmFactoryBean provided by Spring must be registered first. In addition, JtaTransactionManager, which provides distributed transactions, can be used as TransactionManager.

In addition, to process distributed transactions, DataSource that provides distributed transactions must be used. org.enhydra.jdbc.pool.StandardXAPoolDataSource provided by JOTM can be used, but this document describes how to process distributed transactions by using Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseXADataSource.

The following is an example of processing distributed transactions by using org.springframework.transaction.jta.JtaTransactionManager and Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseXADataSource.

1. Specify DataSource by using the AltibaseXADataSource
2. Specify JotmFactoryBean
3. Specify JtaTransactionManager as TransactionManager
4. Specify the bean that processes the declarative transaction by using the TransactionProxyFactoryBean class.

Ex) applicationContext.xml file of XAConnection

```
…
<bean id="dataSource1" class="Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseXADataSource">
   <!-- connection url-->
   <property name="url" value="jdbc:Altibase://192.168.1.35:21129/mydb"/>
   <!-- DB user account setting -->
   <property name="user" value="sys"/>
   <!-- DB user password setting -->
   <property name="password" value="manager" />
</bean>

<bean id="dataSource2" class="Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseXADataSource">
   <!-- connection url-->
   <property name="url" value="jdbc:Altibase://127.0.0.1:20300/mydb"/>
   <!-- DB user account setting -->
<property name="user" value="sys"/>
   <!-- DB user password setting -->
<property name="password" value="manager" />
</bean>

<bean id="accountDao1" class="com.altibase.banking.AccountDao">
   <property name="dataSource" ref="dataSource1"/>
</bean>

<bean id="accountDao2" class="com.altibase.banking.AccountDao">
   <property name="dataSource" ref="dataSource2"/>
</bean>

<bean id="jotm" class="org.springframework.transaction.jta.JotmFactoryBean"/>

<bean id="transactionManager"
    class="org.springframework.transaction.jta.JtaTransactionManager">
<property name="userTransaction" ref="jotm"/>
</bean>

<bean id="txProxyTemplate" abstract="true" class="org.springframework.transaction.interceptor.TransactionProxyFactoryBean">
   <property name="transactionManager"  ref="transactionManager" />
   <property name="transactionAttributes">
    <props>
        <prop key="get*">PROPAGATION_REQUIRED, readOnly</prop>
        <prop key="add*">PROPAGATION_REQUIRED</prop>
    </props>
   </property>
</bean>

<bean id="accountService" parent="txProxyTemplate">
<property name="target">
       <bean class="com.altibase.banking.AccountService">
            <property name="accountDao1" ref="accountDao1"/>
            <property name="accountDao2" ref="accountDao2"/>
       </bean>
   </property>
</bean>
…
```

In order to run the XAConnection project included in the example, jar files for JOTM must be added in addition to the jar files previously added.

![transaction_1.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/6.%20Transaction%20Manager/transaction_1.png?api=v2)

The files related to JOTM can be downloaded from [http://forge.ow2.org/projects/jotm/](http://forge.ow2.org/projects/jotm/).

After downloading and extracting, there are jar files. Among them, add carol-2.0.5.jar, connector-1_5.jar, howl-0.1.11.jar, jotm.jar, jta-spec1_0_1.jar, and xapool-1.5.0.jar files to the project. (The name of the jar file above may be different depending on the downloaded version of JOTM.)

Other cglib-nodep-2.1.3.jar files are required separately.
