# 7. Considerations/Notes for Spring Integration
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=14058445
Updated: 2025-09-23T10:15:03.000+0900

- [LOB Data Processing](#id-7.Considerations/NotesforSpringIntegration-LOBDataProcessing)

This chapter describes considerations when integrating Altibase in Spring.

## LOB Data Processing

In order to process LOB data in ALTIBASE, the user must explicitly manage the transaction after changing the autocommit mode to false. Therefore, in order to process LOB in Spring, TransactionManager bean must be specified. In addition, when using a declarative transaction, propagation must be specified as one of PROPAGATION_REQUIRED, PROPAGATION_REQUIRES_NEW, and PROPAGATION_NESTED.

If TransactionManager is not specified, or if declarative transaction propagation is set to a value other than those described above, LOB queries may return null, or an error such as "java.sql.SQLException: [0]:LobLocator can not span the transaction 101858625." may occur. The same error can occur when inserting LOB data.

Ex) applicationContext.xml file of LobConnection

```
…
<bean id="transactionManager"
class="org.springframework.jdbc.datasource.DataSourceTransactionManager">
    <property name="dataSource" ref="dataSource"/>
</bean>

<bean id="txProxyTemplate" abstract="true"
class="org.springframework.transaction.interceptor.TransactionProxyFactoryBean">
    <property name="transactionManager"  ref="transactionManager" />
    <property name="transactionAttributes">
    <props>
        <prop key="get*">PROPAGATION_REQUIRED</prop>
        <prop key="add*">PROPAGATION_ REQUIRED </prop>
    </props>
    </property>

</bean>

<bean id="lobSampleService" parent="txProxyTemplate">
<property name="target">
         <bean class="com.altibase.lob.LobSampleService">
              <property name="lobSampleDao" ref="lobSampleDao"/>
         </bean>
    </property>
</bean>
…
```

# 8. Appendix - HelloSpring
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/8.+Appendix+-+HelloSpring
Updated: 2025-09-23T10:15:21.000+0900

- [HelloSpring Implementation](#id-8.Appendix-HelloSpring-HelloSpringImplementation) - [1. Creating HelloSpring project](#id-8.Appendix-HelloSpring-1.CreatingHelloSpringproject) - [2. Implementing sample Java file](#id-8.Appendix-HelloSpring-2.ImplementingsampleJavafile) - [3. Defining bean configuration](#id-8.Appendix-HelloSpring-3.Definingbeanconfiguration) - [4. Defining HelloApp class](#id-8.Appendix-HelloSpring-4.DefiningHelloAppclass) - [5. Adding related jar files](#id-8.Appendix-HelloSpring-5.Addingrelatedjarfiles) - [6. Running the HelloSpring project](#id-8.Appendix-HelloSpring-6.RunningtheHelloSpringproject)

Based on the sample example, this appendix describes how to use Spring in more detail.

The name of the sample project described in the appendix is HelloSpring, and it was created in Eclipse.

HelloSpring project is a simple program that prints a greeting message. It prints the greeting message defined in the bean by importing the bean (greetingService) defined in the bean configuration file (applicationContext.xml) from the Spring container (BeanFactory).

## **HelloSpring Implementation**

### **1. Creating HelloSpring project**

---

1-1. Click Menu - File - Java Project.
1-2. Project name: enter HelloSpring.
1-3. Click the Finish button.

![additional_1.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/8.%20Appendix%20-%20HelloSpring/additional_1.png?api=v2)

### **2. Implementing sample Java file**

---

Implement the following class and interface.

**2-1. GreetingService interface**

This is the interface that defines the service.

Right-click the HelloSpring project's src directory and click New – Interface.

Enter com.altibase.hello for Package: and GreetingService for Name:.

![additional_2.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/8.%20Appendix%20-%20HelloSpring/additional_2.png?api=v2)

When the GreetingService.java file is created, write the source as follows.

**GreetingService.java**

```
package com.altibase.hello;

public interface GreetingService {
    public void sayGreeting();
}
```

**2-2. GreetingServiceImp class**

This class implements the GreetingService interface.

Right-click the HelloSpring project's src directory and click New-Class.

Enter com.altibase.hello for Package: and GreetingServiceImp for Name:

Click Add button next to Interfaces:, enter GreetingService, and then click the OK button.

![additional_3.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/8.%20Appendix%20-%20HelloSpring/additional_3.png?api=v2)

When the GreetingServiceImp.java file is created, write the source as follows.

**GreetingServiceImp.java**

```
 package com.altibase.hello;

public class GreetingServiceImp implements GreetingService{
    private String greeting;
    public GreetingServiceImp(){

    }
    public GreetingServiceImp(String greeting){
        this.greeting = greeting;
    }
    public void sayGreeting() {
        System.out.println(greeting);
    }
    public void setGreeting(String greeting){
        this.greeting = greeting;
    }
}
```

### **3. Defining bean configuration**

---

Define bean for GreetingServiceImp in the bean configuration file (applicationContext.xml).

Right-click the HelloSpring project and click New – File.

Create applicationContext.xml in File name:.

![additional_4.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/8.%20Appendix%20-%20HelloSpring/additional_4.png?api=v2)

Write the following in the applicationContext.xml file.

**applicationContext.xml**

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<beans xmlns="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
xmlns:context="http://www.springframework.org/schema/context"
xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans/spring-beans-3.2.xsd
http://www.springframework.org/schema/context http://www.springframework.org/schema/context/spring-context-3.2.xsd">

  <bean id="greetingService" class="com.altibase.hello.GreetingServiceImp">
        <property name="greeting">
            <value>Hello</value>
        </property>
  </bean>

</beans>
```

greetingService is the name of the bean. This can be used by importing the bean with the corresponding name in the java program.

In the class, specify the full name of the GreetingServiceImp class in charge of the service, and put the message to be set in the member variable greeting defined in GreetingServiceImp in the property.

### **4. Defining HelloApp class**

---

As the main class, get the bean defined GreetingServiceImp from the BeanFactory and call the service method (sayGreeting()).

Right-click the HelloSpring project's src directory and click New-Class.

Leave the Package: part blank and enter HelloApp in Name:.

**![additional_5.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/8.%20Appendix%20-%20HelloSpring/additional_5.png?api=v2)**

When the HelloApp.java file is created, write the source as follows.

**HelloApp.java**

```
 import org.springframework.context.ApplicationContext;
import org.springframework.context.support.ClassPathXmlApplicationContext;

import com.altibase.hello.GreetingService;
public class HelloApp {

    /**
     * @param args
     */
    public static void main(String[] args) {

        @SuppressWarnings("resource")
        ApplicationContext factory = new ClassPathXmlApplicationContext("applicationContext.xml");

        GreetingService greetingService = (GreetingService)factory.getBean("greetingService");
        greetingService.sayGreeting();
    }
}
```

The source applicationContext.xml above is the bean configuration file defined above, and greetingService represents the bean name for the GreetingServiceImp class defined in applicationContext.xml.

### **5. Adding related jar files**

---

Add Spring related jar file to HelloSpring.

Right-click on HelloSpring project and click Properties – Java Build Path – Add External in Libraries

Click JARS to add spring.jar file and common-logging.jar file among Spring Framework jar files.

Please refer to the description of DriverManagerDataSource for the location of the file.

![additional_6.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/8.%20Appendix%20-%20HelloSpring/additional_6.png?api=v2)

### **6. Running the HelloSpring project**

After clicking the HelloSpring project, run it from the menu or click the "Run" button.

The Hello string is printed in the console window.

**![additional_7.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/8.%20Appendix%20-%20HelloSpring/additional_7.png?api=v2)**
<!-- SOURCE_BLOCK_END source_id="AID-SRC-000391" block_id="BLOCK-000383" -->

# Spring Integration Guide for Altibase
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/Spring+Integration+Guide+for+Altibase
Updated: 2020-07-31T15:19:35.000+0900

# Overview

This technical document describes how to integrate with Altibase and Spring. In this document, Spring Framework 3.2.x and ALTIBASE 6.3.1 were used, Eclipse as the development IDE. Examples are provided for each chapter in addition to the document.

For errors and improvements related to this document, please contact the technical support portal or technical support center

- Technical support portal: [http://support.altibase.com](http://support.altibase.com/) > Technical Knowledge > Q&A
- Technical support center: 02-2082-1114

Old Version: ALTIBASE_Spring_Integration Guide_2.5.pdf (spring v2.5)

In addition to this document, please refer to the following technical documents for reference.

1. Altibase Development Guide
2. Java Development Guide
3. JBOSS Integration Guide for Altibase
4. TOMCAT Integration Guide for Altibase
5. WEBSPHERE Integration Guide for Altibase
6. WEBLOGIC Integration Guide for Altibase
7. Hibernate Integration Guide for Altibase
8. iBatis Integration Guide for Altibase

# 1. TOMCAT Installation
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/1.+TOMCAT+Installation
Updated: 2021-02-18T17:17:02.000+0900

- [Downloading TOMCAT](#id-1.TOMCATInstallation-DownloadingTOMCAT) - [Installing TOMCAT](#id-1.TOMCATInstallation-InstallingTOMCAT) - [Setting environment variables](#id-1.TOMCATInstallation-Settingenvironmentvariables) - [Running TOMCAT](#id-1.TOMCATInstallation-RunningTOMCAT) - [Shutting TOMCAT down](#id-1.TOMCATInstallation-ShuttingTOMCATdown)

---

Let's take a brief look at how to install TOMCAT. Let's install the TOMCAT 7 product.

Before installing the TOMCAT, Java Development Kit (JDK) or Java Runtime Environment (JRE) must be installed.

## **Downloading TOMCAT**

Go to [http://tomcat.apache.org/download-70.cgi](http://tomcat.apache.org/download-70.cgi) site and download the recently released TOMCAT binary file (apache-tomcat-7.0.56.tar.gz).

![download.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/1.%20TOMCAT%20Installation/download.png?api=v2)

## **Installing TOMCAT**

Move the downloaded compressed file to FTP. (tomcat installation account)

Extract the uploaded compressed file to the appropriate directory. (tar xvzf apache-tomcat-7.0.56.tar.gz).

Because it is a binary, the installation is finished by extracting it.

```
[tomcat@dev ~]$ tar xvzf apache-tomcat-7.0.56.tar.gz
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/bin/catalina.sh
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/bin/configtest.sh
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/bin/daemon.sh
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/bin/digest.sh
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/bin/setclasspath.sh
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/bin/shutdown.sh
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/bin/startup.sh
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/bin/tool-wrapper.sh
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/bin/version.sh
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/conf/
.
.
.
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/webapps/manager/images/tomcat.gif
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/webapps/manager/images/update.gif
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/webapps/manager/images/void.gif
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/webapps/manager/index.jsp
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/webapps/manager/status.xsd
apache-tomcat-7.0.56/webapps/manager/xform.xsl
[tomcat@dev ~]$ mv apache-tomcat-7.0.56 /app/was/tomcat7
```

<Example of tomcat installation>

## **Setting environment variables**

Set the following environment variables.

1. CATALINA_HOME: Specify the directory where TOMCAT is installed.

2. JAVA_HOME or JRE_HOME: Specify the directory where JDK or JRE is installed.

3. PATH: Add the $CATALINA_HOME/bin directory (the path of the bin directory under the TOMCAT installation directory set in step 1) to the PATH.

```
[tomcat@dev ~]$ vi .bash_profile
export CATALINA_HOME=/app/was/tomcat7
export JAVA_HOME=/app/java/jdk1.6
export PATH=$CATALINA_HOME/bin:$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH

[tomcat@dev ~]$ . .bash_profile
```

<Example of Linux configuraiton>

## **Running TOMCAT**

Execute the following command to start the TOMCAT.

```
$ catalina.sh start (windows : catalina start)
[tomcat@dev ~]$ catalina.sh start
Using CATALINA_BASE:   /app/was/tomcat7
Using CATALINA_HOME:   /app/was/tomcat7
Using CATALINA_TMPDIR: /app/was/tomcat7/temp
Using JRE_HOME:        /app/java/jdk1.6
Using CLASSPATH:       /app/was/tomcat7/bin/bootstrap.jar:/app/was/tomcat7/bin/tomcat-juli.jar
Tomcat started.
[tomcat@dev ~]$
```

## **Shutting TOMCAT down**

Execute the following command to shutdown TOMCAT.

```
$ catalina.sh stop (windows : catalina stop)
[tomcat@dev ~]$ catalina.sh stop
Using CATALINA_BASE:   /app/was/tomcat7
Using CATALINA_HOME:   /app/was/tomcat7
Using CATALINA_TMPDIR: /app/was/tomcat7/temp
Using JRE_HOME:        /app/java/jdk1.6
Using CLASSPATH:       /app/was/tomcat7/bin/bootstrap.jar:/app/was/tomcat7/bin/tomcat-juli.jar
[tomcat@dev ~]$
```

# 2. JDBC Driver Configuration
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/2.+JDBC+Driver+Configuration
Updated: 2021-02-18T17:17:43.000+0900

- [How to get the ALTIBASE JDBC driver file](#id-2.JDBCDriverConfiguration-HowtogettheALTIBASEJDBCdrivefile) - [How to check the ALTIBASE JDBC driver version](#id-2.JDBCDriverConfiguration-HowtochecktheALTIBASEJDBCdriverversion) - [Location of JDBC driver file in TOMCAT](#id-2.JDBCDriverConfiguration-LocationofJDBCdrivefileinTOMCAT)

---

In the TOMCAT, the ALTIBASE JDBC driver must be placed in an appropriate location to integrate with ALTIBASE.

## **How to get the ALTIBASE JDBC driver file**

The JDBC driver provided by ALTIBASE is Altibase.jar. This file is located in the $ALTIBASE_HOME/lib directory of the server where ALTIBASE is installed.

Starting from Altibase version 5 or later, Altibase.jar and Altibase5.jar files exist in the $ALTIBASE_HOME/lib directory. Altibase.jar is a JDBC driver file, and Altibase5.jar is used when integrating Altibase version 5 and lower. Therefore, in order to integrate with one ALTIBASE DB or multiple ALTIBASE DBs of the same version, $ALTIBASE_HOME/lib/Altibase.jar file can be used.

## **How to check the ALTIBASE JDBC driver version**

To check the ALTIBASE JDBC driver version, execute the following command.

```
[altibase@dev lib]$ java -jar Altibase.jar
 JDBC Driver Info : Altibase Ver = 6.3.1.2.1 for JavaVM v1.4, CMP:7.1.1, Aug 18 2014 15:36:32
```

In order to check whether the ALTIBASE DB server and the ALTIBASE JDBC Driver that are to be integrated are compatible, checking the ALTIBASE DB server version is required. In this case, if the cm protocol version of the ALTIBASE DB server and the CMP of the ALTIBASE JDBC Driver is the same, they are compatible.

```
[altibase@dev lib]$ altibase -v
version 6.3.1.2.1 X86_64_LINUX_redhat_Enterprise_ES4-64bit-6.3.1.2.1-release-GCC3.4.6
(x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) Aug 18 2014 15:45:00, binary db version 6.2.1,
meta version 6.3.1, cm protocol version 7.1.1, replication protocol version 7.4.1
```

As the version is upgraded, there is a possibility that a bug related to JDBC has been fixed. Generally, it is recommended to match the ALTIBASE DB server version with the ALTIBASE JDBC driver version or use the latest ALTIBASE JDBC driver file.

## **Location of JDBC driver file in TOMCAT**

In order to integrate ALTIBASE and TOMCAT, the ALTIBASE JDBC driver (`Altibase.jar`) should be located in an appropriate place so that it can be recognized automatically by TOMCAT.

1. Add Altibase.jar to CLASSPATH.

```
[tomcat@dev ~]$ cd $CATALINA_HOME/bin
[tomcat@dev bin]$ vi catalina.sh
CLASSPATH=/app/db/ALTIBASE/lib/Altibase.jar

[tomcat@dev bin]$ catalina.sh stop
Using CATALINA_BASE:   /app/was/tomcat7
Using CATALINA_HOME:   /app/was/tomcat7
Using CATALINA_TMPDIR: /app/was/tomcat7/temp
Using JRE_HOME:        /app/java/jdk1.6
Using CLASSPATH:       /app/db/ALTIBASE/lib/Altibase.jar:
/app/was/tomcat7/bin/bootstrap.jar:/app/was/tomcat7/bin/tomcat-juli.jar
[tomcat@dev bin]$ catalina.sh start
Using CATALINA_BASE:   /app/was/tomcat7
Using CATALINA_HOME:   /app/was/tomcat7
Using CATALINA_TMPDIR: /app/was/tomcat7/temp
Using JRE_HOME:        /app/java/jdk1.6
Using CLASSPATH:       /app/db/ALTIBASE/lib/Altibase.jar:
/app/was/tomcat7/bin/bootstrap.jar:/app/was/tomcat7/bin/tomcat-juli.jar
Tomcat started.
```

2. Altibase.jar is located in the $CATALINA_HOME/lib directory.

```
[tomcat@dev ~]$cd $CATALINA_HOME/lib
[tomcat@dev lib]$ cp /app/db/ALTIBASE/lib/Altibase.jar ./
[tomcat@dev lib]$
```
<!-- SOURCE_BLOCK_END source_id="AID-SRC-000395" block_id="BLOCK-000386" -->

# 3. Integrating ALTIBASE and TOMCAT
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/3.+Integrating+ALTIBASE+and+TOMCAT
Updated: 2021-02-18T17:22:25.000+0900

- [JNDI DataSource Integration](#id-3.IntegratingALTIBASEandTOMCAT-JNDIDataSourceIntegration) - [Integration with general JDBC method](#id-3.IntegratingALTIBASEandTOMCAT-IntegrationwithgeneralJDBCmethod)

---

This chapter describes how to integrate ALTIBASE and TOMCAT.

The available integration approaches include DBCP, the general JDBC method, and Altibase ConnectionPool.

## **JNDI DataSource Integration**

To configure JNDI DataSource, write the following in $CATALINA_HOME/conf/context.xml.

```
$CATALINA_HOME/conf/context.xml
< context>
<Resource name="jdbc/Altibase" auth="Container"
type="javax.sql.DataSource"
driverClassName="Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver"
url="jdbc:Altibase://127.0.0.1:20300/mydb"
username="sys" password="manager"
maxActive="3" maxIdle="2" initialSize="1"
defaultAutoCommit="false"
removeAbandoned="true" logAbandoned="true"
removeAbandonedTimeout="60"
validationQuery="select 1 from dual"/>
</context>
```

It can be used on the web by adding the following contents to the web application home/WEB-INF/web.xml.

Web application home/WEB-INF/web.xml

```
<resource-ref>
<description>DB Connection</description>
<res-ref-name>jdbc/Altibase</res-ref-name>
<res-type>javax.sql.DataSource</res-type>
<res-auth>Container</res-auth>
</resource-ref>

<Resource>
```

The properties defined in the tag are as follows.

| driverClassName | Altibase JDBC driver class name |
| --- | --- |
| url | Connection string information for connecting to Altibase. Enter it in the form `jdbc:Altibase://IP:port_no/db_name`. |
| Username | The database account |
| Password | The database password |
| maxActive | The maximum number of connections, 0 is unlimited. The default is 8. |
| initialSize | The initial size of connections. The default is 0. |
| maxIdle | The maximum number of connections that wait in the pool. The default is 8. |
| minIdle | The minimum number of connections that wait in the pool. The default is 0. |
| maxWait | The maximum connection attempt time (unit: millisec) -1 waits indefinitely. The default: infinite waiting. |
| validationQuery | The SQL statement used to check the validation of connection<br>Must be specified as a select statement that returns at least one row<br>Ex) select 1 from dual |
| defaultAutoCommit | Sets autocommit mode. The default: true. |
| defaultTransactionIsolation | Sets Transaction Isolation level.<br>The values `NONE`, `REPEATABLE_READ`, and `SERIALIZABLE` can be set, and the default follows the default value of the DB server.<br>The isolation level of ALTIBASE is `READ COMMITTED` by default. |
| removeAbandoned | Determines the removal function for the abandoned connection. The default is false.<br>When the connection is removed, the number of connections exceeds the value set for maxActive and is requested for connection.<br>The connection can be assigned when maxActive is not reached, abandoned connection removal does not occur. |
| removeAbandonedTimeout | Sets the time for removal of abandoned timeout. The default is 300. |
| logAbandoned | Determines whether to abandon stack information in the log when removing abandoned connections. The default is false. |

In the program, obtain the connection with the JNDI DataSource as follows.

In this case, java:/comp/env is a prefix used when looking up JNDI.

```
Context envContext  = (Context)new InitialContext().lookup("java:/comp/env");
DataSource ds = (DataSource)envContext.lookup("jdbc/Altibase");
Connection conn = ds.getConnection();
```

Or

```
Context initCtx = new InitialContext();
DataSource ds =  (DataSource)initCtx.lookup("java:comp/env/jdbc/Altibase");
Connection conn = ds.getConnection();
```

The following is a JSP example program that integrates with ALTIBASE using the JNDI DataSource set above.

```
<%@ page import="java.sql.*, javax.naming.*, javax.sql.*"%>
<%
Context initCtx = new InitialContext();
DataSource ds =  (DataSource)initCtx.lookup("java:comp/env/jdbc/Altibase");
Connection conn = ds.getConnection();
Statement stmt = conn.createStatement();
String query = "select to_char(sysdate,'yyyy/mm/dd hh24:mi:ss') from dual";
ResultSet rs = stmt.executeQuery(query);
if(rs.next()) {
     out.println(rs.getString(1));
}
rs.close();
stmt.close();
conn.close();
%>
```

## **Integration with general JDBC method**

1. Load the JDBC driver.
2. Get the Connection object.
3. Get the Statement object.
4. Execute the SQL statement and place it in the ResultSet.
5. Close all related objects after the operation is completed.

The following is a JSP example program that integrates with Altibase using the general JDBC method.

```
<%@page import="java.sql.ResultSet"%>
<%@page import="java.sql.Statement"%>
<%@page import="java.sql.DriverManager"%>
<%@page import="java.sql.Connection"%>
<%@page import="java.util.Properties"%>
<%
Class.forName("Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver");
Properties prop = new Properties();
prop.put("user", "sys");
prop.put("password", "manager");
String url = "jdbc:Altibase://192.168.56.110:20300/mydb";
String sql = "SELECT TO_CHAR(SYSDATE,'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS') FROM DUAL";

Connection conn = null;
Statement stmt= null;
ResultSet rs = null;
try {
conn = DriverManager.getConnection(url, prop);
stmt = conn.createStatement();
rs = stmt.executeQuery(sql);
while(rs.next()) {
        out.println(rs.getString(1));
}
}catch(Exception se) {
out.println(se.getMessage());
} finally {
    rs.close();
    stmt.close();
    conn.close();
}
%>
```

# 4. Fail-Over Configuration
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/4.+Fail-Over+Configuration
Updated: 2021-02-18T17:23:35.000+0900

- [FailOver Configuration](#id-4.Fail-OverConfiguration-FailOverConfiguration)

---

This chapter describes how to integrate with TOMCAT using the FailOver function provided by ALTIBASE.

## **FailOver Configuration**

TOMCAT does not provide a FailOver function. However, because ALTIBASE provides FailOver starting from Altibase v5.3.3, FailOver can be implemented by using the ALTIBASE FailOver function.

How to use is as follows.

1. When specifying a JNDI DataSource in the `context.xml` file, specify the FailOver-related properties in the Connection URL part.

```
<context>
<Resource name="jdbc/Altibase" auth="Container" type="javax.sql.DataSource"
driverClassName="Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver"
maxActive="100" maxIdle="-1" maxWait="-1"
username="sys" password="manager"
url="jdbc:Altibase://192.168.6.224:21129/mydb?
AlternateServers=(192.168.1.35:21129)&
ConnectionRetryCount=3&
ConnectionRetryDelay=3&
SessionFailOver=off&
LoadBalance=off"
validationQuery="SELECT 1 FROM DUAL" testOnBorrow="true"
removeAbandoned="true" removeAbandonedTimeout="60"
logAbandoned="true" />
</context>
```

- Refer to the FailOver/server.xml file

FailOver related properties are as follows. For more detailed information, please refer to the Replication Manual.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| AlternateServer | Indicates the alternate servers to be connected when a failure occurs (IP Address1:Port1, IP Address2:Port2,...). |
| ConnectionRetryCount | The number of tries of connection attempts when an alternative server connection fails. |
| ConnectionRetryDelay | Time to wait before attempting to connect when the alternative server connection fails (in seconds) |
| LoadBalance | When set to on, random selection is made including default server and alternate servers when the first connection is attempted. If set to off, it connects to the default server when it tries to connect for the first time, and if it fails, it connects to the server described by AlternateServer. |
| SessionFailOver | Indicates whether to perform STF (Service Time Fail-Over)<br>on : STF, off : CTF The CTF (Connection Time Fail-Over) recognizes a failure at the time of DBMS connection and connects to the DBMS of another available node instead of the DBMS where the failure occurred and proceeds with the service. STF (Service Time Fail-Over) means that a failure occurs during service by successfully connecting to the DBMS, accessing the DBMS of another available node to restore the properties of the session, and then performing the task logic of the user application again. That is, it is the case that it is necessary to perform the operation performed in the DBMS where the failure occurred once again. |

For the implementation method of CTF and STF, please refer to the FailOver technical document.
<!-- SOURCE_BLOCK_END source_id="AID-SRC-000397" block_id="BLOCK-000388" -->

# 5. Considerations when integrating TOMCAT
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/5.+Considerations+when+integrating+TOMCAT
Updated: 2025-10-21T09:49:16.000+0900

- [JDK environment when using TOMCAT](#id-5.ConsiderationswhenintegratingTOMCAT-JDKenvironmentwhenusingTOMCAT) - [Return of used resource](#id-5.ConsiderationswhenintegratingTOMCAT-Returnofusedresource) - [Remove abandoned connection](#id-5.ConsiderationswhenintegratingTOMCAT-Removeabandonedconnection)

---

This chapter describes considerations when integrating TOMCAT.

## **JDK environment when using TOMCAT**

When processing prepared statements using DBCP, if `testOnBorrow` (default: true) or `poolPrepareStatements` (default: false) is changed to improve performance, using JDK/JRE 1.6 or later is recommended.

Symptoms of the problem

Tomcat log (version 6)

```
--- Check the statement (query failed).

--- Cause: java.sql.SQLException: [0]:Failure to find statement; nested exception is com.ibatis.common.jdbc.exception.NestedSQLException:

--- The error occurred in maps/CommonSqlMap.xml.

--- The error occurred while applying a parameter map.

--- Check the Common.getIservSp-InlineParameterMap.

--- Check the statement (query failed).

--- Cause: java.sql.SQLException: [0]:Failure to find statement
```

If it is normal,

```
Tomcat log (version 6)

[0001][14:14:31 386][    2][    0] GET-CONNECTION[org.apache.tomcat.dbcp.dbcp.BasicDataSource.getConnection] [1 ms]
```

How to check

```
After removing the comment at the bottom of the contents of the $CATALINA_HOME/conf/server.xml file, restart Tomcat and check $CATALINA_HOME/logs/tomcat.log.
 Before the change>
        <!--
        <Valve className="org.apache.catalina.valves.AccessLogValve"
                 directory="logs"  prefix="localhost_access_log." suffix=".txt"
                 pattern="common" resolveHosts="false"/>
        -->

After the change>
        <Valve className="org.apache.catalina.valves.AccessLogValve"
                 directory="logs"  prefix="localhost_access_log." suffix=".txt"
                 pattern="%a %b %t %s %D %r " resolveHosts="false"/>
```

Reference: [http://tomcat.apache.org/tomcat-5.5-doc/config/valve.html](http://tomcat.apache.org/tomcat-5.5-doc/config/valve.html)

Recommended Tomcat settings

|  | Environment 1 | Environment 2 | Environment 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JDK Ver | 1.5 | 1.6 | 1.6 |
| Tomcat Ver | 6 (dbcp ver 1.3) | 6 (dbcp ver 1.3) | 7 (dbcp ver 1.4) |
| testOnBorrow | Only TRUE is recommended (Default) | True/False | True/False |
| poolPrepareStatements | Only FALSE recommended (Default) | True/False | True/False |
| Result | `testOnBorrow=False` and `poolPrepareStatements=true` are not recommended.<br>Upgrade to JRE or JDK 1.6 is recommended. | Recommended | Recommended |

- testOnBorrow
  + When getting a connection from the connection pool, the connection is validated
  + The default value is false, and the default value is generally used. If set to true, validationQuery is executed every time, so a slight performance decrease is expected.
- poolPrepareStatements
  + Statement pooling is maintained for each connection in DBCP, so the application server (App) keeps the information compiled for the query. After that, it is possible to improve performance by repeating only the execute step without preparing the same query

## **Return of used resource**

Connection, Statement, and ResultSet allocated by the program must be explicitly closed after use. If it is not closed, resources are continuously allocated during the life cycle of the variable that declared the above resource, which results in unnecessary resource consumption.

If the connection is not closed, the connection will not be returned to the pool, so it will be unable to use it elsewhere.

Statement information is allocated and remained in memory not only on the application but also on the DB server while the session is maintained. Therefore, if the statement and the connection are not closed, this could be a problem for unnecessary resources are continuously allocated in the application, but the Query_Prepare memory area of the DB server also increases.

If the above resources are not explicitly closed, they remain allocated in memory during the life cycle of the variable that declares the resource. When the life cycle ends, the resource is no longer referenced, so the JVM (Java Virtual Machine) GC (Garbage Collector) will eventually release it. However, GC is generally the lowest-priority thread, so it is difficult to predict when GC will release the resource. In other words, even after the variable life cycle ends and the application no longer references the resource, it cannot be released immediately, and the DB server keeps the resource information until GC releases it.

Therefore, it is recommended to close the used resource explicitly.

## **Remove abandoned connection**

When processing connections using DBCP, the web application must explicitly close `ResultSet`, `Statement`, and `Connection`. If the web application fails to close these resources, they cannot be reused later. This is called a connection pool leak, and if the leak continues, all available connections will eventually be exhausted. To prevent this problem, DBCP provides a method for recovering and logging connections that have been abandoned due to a problem. Set the following property.

```
removeAbandoned="true"
```

# 6. Errors when integrating TOMCAT
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/6.+Errors+when+integrating+TOMCAT
Updated: 2021-02-18T17:25:33.000+0900

- [No suitable driver](#id-6.ErrorswhenintegratingTOMCAT-Nosuitabledriver) - [Communication link failure](#id-6.ErrorswhenintegratingTOMCAT-Communicationlinkfailure) - [Others](#id-6.ErrorswhenintegratingTOMCAT-Others)

---

This chapter describes the contents of errors when integrating ALTIBASE and TOMCAT.

## **No suitable driver**

java.sql.SQLException: No suitable driver error occurs when the part corresponding to the Altibase of connection URL information is incorrectly entered.

```
url="jdbc:mysql://127.0.0.1:20300/mydb"
An error occurs because the jdbc:Altibase part is incorrectly set as the jdbc:mysql part.
```

## **Communication link failure**

java.sql.SQLException: Communication link failure error occurs in the following situations:

1. When the ALTIBASE DB server is not running

2. When the ALTIBASE JDBC driver file is different from the version of the ALTIBASE DB server.

Ex) The version of the ALTIBASE DB server is 5.3.1, but when using the 5.1.1 version of the ALTIBASE JDBC driver file

3. When the connection URL information is set incorrectly

3-1. When the IP is set incorrectly

3-2. When the PORT_NO is set incorrectly

Ex) When the IP address of the ALTIBASE DB server is 10.10.10.10 and PORT_NO is 20300, but the IP address is set to 10.10.10.1 or PORT_NO is set to 20301.

```
url="jdbc:Altibase://10.10.10.1:20301/mydb"
```

## **Others**

Occasionally, when a DataSource is specified in the context.xml file of a web application, it may be possible to encounter a client unable to establish a connection error or an error that the driver class is null even though the connection URL part is correct. In this case, delete the web application name.xml file in the $CATALINA_HOME/conf/catalina directory. Occasionally, even though the context.xml file of a web application has been changed, an error occurs because the file is not reloading.

# 0. Prerequisites
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/0.+Prerequisites
Updated: 2025-09-24T09:08:46.000+0900

- [WebLogic Version](#id-0.Prerequisites-WebLogicVersion) - [JDBC Specification](#id-0.Prerequisites-JDBCSpecification)

### WebLogic Version

We recommend to use the latest version, and at least WebLogic 8.1.6.0 or later is recommended.

If a different version of Altibase is integrated at a lower version than this, the JDBC driver integration may not work properly, which may cause the operation of the WebLogic server instance to fail or hang.

### JDBC Specification

The Altibase 5 JDBC driver was built in JDK 1.4 based on the JDBC specification 3.0 (JRE 1.4 or 1.5), and returns "Not supported" or an error in case of non-spec support.

Even with JDBC specification 3.0, some specifications are not supported, so check unsupported specifications in the API Manual in advance. Altibase does not guarantee issues caused by unsupported specifications.

Therefore, an application program written on the basis of JDBC specification 4.0 (JRE 1.6 or later) may cause problems due to unsupported specifications, so it is necessary to comply with JDBC 3.0 specification from the development stage.
<!-- SOURCE_BLOCK_END source_id="AID-SRC-000407" block_id="BLOCK-000392" -->

# 1. WebLogic Setup
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/1.+WebLogic+Setup
Updated: 2025-09-24T09:08:56.000+0900

- [Download](#id-1.WebLogicSetup-Download) - [Installation](#id-1.WebLogicSetup-Installation) - [Creating Domain](#id-1.WebLogicSetup-CreatingDomain)

A brief procedure to create a domain after downloading and installing WebLogic will be described using WebLogic 12.1.3.0 on the Windows platform as an example.

### Download

As BEA Systems, which developed WebLogic in April 2008, was acquired by Oracle, WebLogic can be downloaded from the Oracle middleware product download page from version 9 or later.

[http://www.oracle.com/technetwork/middleware/downloads/index.html](http://www.oracle.com/technetwork/middleware/downloads/index.html)

After accepting the license agreement from the relevant web page, download the most recently released WebLogic for the operating system platform.

![weblogic12c_download.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/1.%20WebLogic%20Setup/weblogic12c_download.png?api=v2)

### Installation

When the downloaded file is running, the WebLogic automatic installer is running.

Install WebLogic in the following procedure.

1.Select Next on the start screen and specify the path where WebLogic and related middleware products will be installed.

![weblogic12c_install1.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/1.%20WebLogic%20Setup/weblogic12c_install1.png?api=v2)![weblogic12c_install2.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/1.%20WebLogic%20Setup/weblogic12c_install2.png?api=v2)![weblogic12c_install3.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/1.%20WebLogic%20Setup/weblogic12c_install3.png?api=v2)

2. Check and Install the installation summary

(The installation path of the WebLogic specified here is later identified by the environment variable WL_HOME.)

![1.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/1.%20WebLogic%20Setup/1.png?api=v2)![2.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/1.%20WebLogic%20Setup/2.png?api=v2)

3. Confirm whether the installation is completed

![3.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/1.%20WebLogic%20Setup/3.png?api=v2)

### Creating Domain

The domain can be created by using the Configuration Wizard.

Install WebLogic in the following procedure.

1.Run the installation wizard to create a new domain. (The user can set the domain location.)

![4.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/1.%20WebLogic%20Setup/4.png?api=v2)![5.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/1.%20WebLogic%20Setup/5.png?api=v2)

2. Enter the user name and password for the management server.

(The installation path of the domain specified here is later identified by the environment variable DOMAIN_HOME.)

![6.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/1.%20WebLogic%20Setup/6.png?api=v2)

3. Set the start mode and JDK of the domain Administration Server.

- Start Mode

For testing purposes, select "Development Mode".

In development mode, web applications can be automatically deployed and changed through `$DOMAIN_HOME/autodeploy`, making testing easier.

- JDK

When the start mode is selected, the appropriate JDK is automatically selected, so it does not need to be selected separately unless there is a special case.

![12.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/1.%20WebLogic%20Setup/12.png?api=v2)

4. If there is a specific change the user wants to make, such as receiving port of the management server, select the relevant item, and change it. If not, skip (NEXT).

For reference, the management server uses port 7001 by default.

![13.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/1.%20WebLogic%20Setup/13.png?api=v2)

5. When domain creation is complete, check the "Start Management Server" option and select Done.

![14.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/1.%20WebLogic%20Setup/14.png?api=v2)

6. Installation Complete

![15.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/1.%20WebLogic%20Setup/15.png?api=v2)
<!-- SOURCE_BLOCK_END source_id="AID-SRC-000408" block_id="BLOCK-000393" -->

# 2. Starting and Shutting Down the WebLogic Server Instance
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/2.+Starting+and+Shutdown+the+WebLogic+Server+Instance
Updated: 2025-09-24T09:09:10.000+0900

- [Start](#start)
- [Shutdown](#shutdown)
- [JDBC Driver Settings](#jdbc-driver-settings)
- [How to get the Altibase JDBC Driver](#how-to-get-the-altibase-jdbc-driver)
- [How to check the Altibase JDBC Driver Version](#how-to-check-the-altibase-jdbc-driver-version)
- [How to set the JDBC Driver to be used in WebLogic](#how-to-set-the-jdbc-driver-to-be-used-in-weblogic)

Among the various ways to start and stop a WebLogic Server instance, this section describes how to use the script or batch files in `$DOMAIN_HOME/bin`.

Each domain provides separate start and stop scripts for the Administration Server and Managed Servers.

- Administration Server: `startWebLogic.cmd`, `stopWebLogic.cmd`
- Managed Server: `startManagedWebLogic.cmd`, `stopManagedWebLogic.cmd`

## Start

Run `startWebLogic.cmd` to start the Administration Server for the domain. The following output shows the message format when startup completes normally.

```
$ startWebLogic.cmd
.
JAVA Memory arguments: -Xms256m -Xmx512m -XX:CompileThreshold=8000 -XX:PermSize=128m  -XX:MaxPermSize=256m
.
***************************************************
*  To start WebLogic Server, use a username and   *
*  password assigned to an admin-level user.  For *
*  server administration, use the WebLogic Server *
*  console at http:\\hostname:port\console        *
***************************************************
... syncopation ...

<2014. 10. 30 4:27:13 PM KST> <Notice> <WebLogicServer> <BEA-000331> <Started the WebLogic Server Administration
 Server "myserver" for domain "mydomain" running in development mode.>
<2014. 10. 30 4:27:13 PM KST> <Notice> <WebLogicServer> <BEA-000360> <The server started in RUNNING mode.>
<2014. 10. 30 4:27:13 PM KST> <Notice> <WebLogicServer> <BEA-000365> <Server state changed to RUNNING.>
```

## Shutdown

Run `stopWebLogic.cmd` to shut down the Administration Server for the domain. The following output shows the message format when shutdown completes normally.

```
$ stopWebLogic.cmd
Stopping Weblogic Server...
... syncopation ...
Connecting to t3://IBM-1DA5AF93847:7001 with userid weblogic ...
Successfully connected to Admin Server 'AdminServer' that belongs to domain 'mydomain'.
... syncopation ...
Shutting down the server AdminServer with force=false while connected to AdminServer ...
Disconnected from weblogic server: AdminServer
Exiting WebLogic Scripting Tool.
Done
Stopping Derby Server...
```

For shutdown, normal termination cannot be guaranteed from the shutdown script result alone.

If the related process still exists even though the shutdown message is normal, check and correct the WebLogic Server instance log.

## **JDBC Driver Settings**

To create a JDBC data source, the relevant JDBC driver must be set in WebLogic. This section describes overall information about JDBC Driver settings.

### How to get the Altibase JDBC Driver

The Altibase JDBC driver is provided as a single file called Altibase.jar.

It is provided with the Altibase Server package by default, so it can be obtained from the `$ALTIBASE_HOME/lib` directory of the operating system account where Altibase is installed.

`Altibase.jar` and `Altibase5.jar` are provided starting from Altibase 5. `Altibase5.jar` is used to connect to Altibase 5 and earlier versions.

Therefore, when only one Altibase server is connected, or when multiple Altibase servers of the same version are connected, use `$ALTIBASE_HOME/lib/Altibase.jar`.

The latest ALTIBASE JDBC driver can be found on [http://support.altibase.com](http://support.altibase.com).

### How to check the Altibase JDBC Driver Version

In order to determine whether the Altibase Server and the Altibase JDBC Driver are compatible, the version of the Altibase Server and Altibase JDBC Driver must be compared to check whether the CM (Communication) protocol matches.

Check the Altibase server version as follows.

```
$ altibase -v
version 6.3.1.2.7 X86_64_LINUX_redhat_Enterprise_ES4-64bit-6.3.1.2.7-release-GCC3.4.6 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) Oct  8 2014 09:16:24, binary db version 6.2.1, meta version 6.3.1, cm protocol version 7.1.1, replication protocol version 7.4.1
```

Check the Altibase JDBC driver version as follows.

```
$ java -jar Altibase.jar
JDBC Driver Info : Altibase Ver = 6.3.1.2.6 for JavaVM v1.4, CMP:7.1.1, Oct  6 2014 13:54:56
```

The Altibase server and Altibase JDBC driver are compatible when the server `cm protocol version` matches the JDBC driver `CMP` value.

Generally, the Altibase JDBC driver file included in the Altibase server package is used for compatibility, but it is recommended to use the latest compatible Altibase JDBC driver file whenever possible.

### How to set the JDBC Driver to be used in WebLogic

To use a specific JDBC driver in WebLogic, the relevant files must be added to the CLASSPATH of the domain management server.

There are two ways to configure it. Either method can be used, but the domain Administration Server must be restarted after configuration.

The following examples configure Altibase 5 and another Altibase version at the same time. When integrating Altibase servers of the same version, only one JDBC driver needs to be configured.

1. Place the JDBC driver files in `$DOMAIN_HOME/lib`.

After the JDBC driver files are placed in `$DOMAIN_HOME/lib`, they are automatically added to the `CLASSPATH` when the domain Administration Server starts. The following message is displayed.

```
...
<2010. 12. 14 4:48:24 PM KST> <Notice> <WebLogicServer> <BEA-000395> <Following extensions directory contents added to the end_of_the_classpath:C:\Oracle\Middleware\user_projects\domains\mydomain\lib\Altibase.jar;C:\Oracle\Middleware\user_projects\domains\mydomain\lib\Altibase5.jar>
...
```

2. Add JDBC driver files directly to the `CLASSPATH` of `startWebLogic.cmd`.

Open `startWebLogic.cmd` for the domain Administration Server, add the JDBC driver files directly to the `CLASSPATH` item, and restart the server.

```
...
set CLASSPATH=%SAVE_CLASSPATH%;C:\WebLogic_lib\Altibase5.jar;C:\WebLogic_lib\Altibase.jar
...
```

# 3. ALTIBASE and WebLogic Integration
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/3.+ALTIBASE+and+WebLogic+Integration
Updated: 2025-09-24T09:09:25.000+0900

- [Creating JDBC Data Source](#id-3.ALTIBASEandWebLogicIntegration-CreatingJDBCDataSource) - [Creating JDBC Data Source](#id-3.ALTIBASEandWebLogicIntegration-CreatingJDBCDataSource.1) - [Change Connection Pool Settings](#id-3.ALTIBASEandWebLogicIntegration-ChangeConnectionPoolSettings) - [Check](#id-3.ALTIBASEandWebLogicIntegration-Check) - [Creating and Deploying Web Application](#id-3.ALTIBASEandWebLogicIntegration-CreatingandDeployingWebApplication) - [Creating Web Application](#id-3.ALTIBASEandWebLogicIntegration-CreatingWebApplication) - [Deploying](#id-3.ALTIBASEandWebLogicIntegration-Deploying) - [Check](#id-3.ALTIBASEandWebLogicIntegration-Check.1) - [Integration Example](#id-3.ALTIBASEandWebLogicIntegration-IntegrationExample) - [ALTIBASE Integration](#id-3.ALTIBASEandWebLogicIntegration-ALTIBASEIntegration) - [Integrating Different Versions of ALTIBASE](#id-3.ALTIBASEandWebLogicIntegration-IntegratingDifferentVersionsofALTIBASE)

This chapter describes the integration procedure for creating a JDBC data source for ALTIBASE to be integrated using the domain management console and then running a simple web application using the JDBC data source.

## Creating JDBC Data Source

This is the procedure for creating a JDBC data source for ALTIBASE and setting up the connection pool of the JDBC data source.

For reference, in the lower version, the connection pool was created first, and then the JDBC data source to use the connection pool was created. However, in the higher version, when the JDBC data source is created, the connection pool is automatically created.

Basically, the JDBC driver setting for the JDBC data source to be created must be performed first by referring to "How to set the JDBC Driver to be used in WebLogic."

### Creating JDBC Data Source

Create a JDBC data source "altibase" for locally installed ALTIBASE.

1.Connect to the management console provided by the domain management server.

[http://127.0.0.1:7001/console](http://127.0.0.1:7001/console)

![console_connection1.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_connection1.png?api=v2)

2. Log in by entering the user name and password of the management server.

![console_connection2.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_connection2.png?api=v2)

3. Select the "Data Source" item on the main page of the management console.

![console_menu1.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_menu1.png?api=v2)

4. Select a general data source from "New".

![console_menu2.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_menu2.png?api=v2)

5. After entering the JDBC data source properties, go to the next step.

- JDBC data source, JNDI name should be the same in general.
- Select the database type "Other".

![console_datasource1.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_datasource1.png?api=v2)

6. Check database type (other)

![console_datasource2.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_datasource2.png?api=v2)

7. Skip the subsequent “JDBC data source attribute” step and go to the next step.

8. Set the "Transaction Options". If there is nothing special to set, go to the next step.

![console_datasource3.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_datasource3.png?api=v2)

9. Enter ALTIBASE information to be linked. (sys / manager)

![console_datasource4.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_datasource4.png?api=v2)

10. Enter the JDBC information related to the connection pool for ALTIBASE connection.

- Driver class name

  When using Altibase.jar, Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver

  When using Altibase#.jar, Altibase#.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver
- URL

  Enter the connection URL based on the information of ALTIBASE entered in the previous step. `jdbc:Altibase://127.0.0.1:20300/mydb`
- Property

  In the case of ALTIBASE 4, the user to access in “user = sys” format must be entered.

  In the case of ALTIBASE 5 and ALTIBASE 6, it can be omitted.
- Test Table
  Generally, a dummy table, dual, is specified.

![console_datasource5.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_datasource5.png?api=v2)

11. Click "Configuration Test" to proceed to the next step if the connection test is successful. If the test fails, refer to the integration error section first.

![console_datasource6.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_datasource6.png?api=v2)

12. Select the management server as the server on which to deploy the JDBC data source, and then select "Done".

![console_datasource7.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_datasource7.png?api=v2)

13. Confirm that the JDBC data source has been successfully added.

![console_datasource10.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_datasource10.png?api=v2)

### Change Connection Pool Settings

When the user creates a JDBC data source, related connection pools are also created. The connection pool has various properties. If necessary, refer to the following procedure to change the settings.

Changing the attributes presented as examples is not mandatory, but is recommended.

1. On the management console main screen, select the "Data Sources" item, select the JDBC data source you want to change, and then select the "Connection Pool" tab of the "Configuration" tab.

![console_datasource11.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_datasource11.png?api=v2)

2. Change the following properties as appropriate and select "Save".

- Initial Capacity
  The default number of connection pools is 1, but a larger number is recommended considering the workload.

### Check

Check whether the JDBC data source creation was successful.

- Check in WebLogic

Select the "Data Source" item on the main screen of management console, click the JDBC data source the user wants to check, and check the connection success on the "Testing" tab of the "Monitoring" tab.

![console_datasource12.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_datasource12.png?api=v2)

- Check in ALTIBASE

Perform a session-related query in ALTIBASE, which is the connection target of the JDBC data source, and check whether the session exists as much as the initial capacity of the established connection pool.

Below is the execution result when the initial capacity is set to 10. The user can see that there are 10 JDBC type sessions.

```
CMD> isql -s 127.0.0.1 -u sys -p manager -port 20300
-----------------------------------------------------------------
     Altibase Client Query utility.
     Release Version 5.3.3.12
     Copyright 2000, ALTIBASE Corporation or its subsidiaries.
     All Rights Reserved.
-----------------------------------------------------------------
ISQL_CONNECTION = TCP, SERVER = 127.0.0.1, PORT_NO = 20300
iSQL> set linesize 200
iSQL> set colsize 20
iSQL> select comm_name, client_type,
   2   db_username, id session_id from v$session;
COMM_NAME             CLIENT_TYPE   DB_USERNAME   SESSION_ID
--------------------------------------------------------------
TCP 127.0.0.1:11274   JDBC          SYS           60
TCP 127.0.0.1:5126    JDBC          SYS           61
TCP 127.0.0.1:8710    JDBC          SYS           63
TCP 127.0.0.1:12294   JDBC          SYS           64
TCP 127.0.0.1:13318   JDBC          SYS           65
TCP 127.0.0.1:18694   JDBC          SYS           66
TCP 127.0.0.1:19462   JDBC          SYS           67
TCP 127.0.0.1:19974   JDBC          SYS           68
TCP 127.0.0.1:20486   JDBC          SYS           69
TCP 127.0.0.1:21254   JDBC          SYS           70
TCP 127.0.0.1:34311   CLI-32LE      SYS           72
11 rows selected.
```

## **Creating and Deploying Web Application**

This is an example of creating and deploying a simple web application for integration.

### **Creating Web Application**

Create a web application named sample and the default page welcome.html.

1.After creating a directory with the name of the web application, create "WEB-INF" as a sub-directory.

![web_inf.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/web_inf.png?api=v2)

2. Create a web.xml file with the following contents in the WEB-INF directory.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE web-app PUBLIC "-//Sun Microsystems, Inc.//DTD Web Application 2.3//EN" "http://java.sun.com/dtd/web-app_2_3.dtd">
<web-app>
  <welcome-file-list>
     <welcome-file>welcome.html</welcome-file>
  </welcome-file-list>
</web-app>
```

### Deploying

The user can manually deploy through the deployment menu provided in the management console, but for convenience, use automatic deployment through $DOMAIN_HOME/autodeploy provided when installed in development mode.

1.Place the entire web application directory created under $DOMAIN_HOME/autodeploy.

![console_deploy1.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_deploy1.png?api=v2)

2. Select the "Deployment" menu on the left side of the main page of the management console to check the automatic deployment.

### Check

The example of the basic page of the web application confirms the success of the deployment.

1.Create welcome.html in the sample directory with the following content.

```
<head><title>Welcome Page</title></head>
<body>welcome!!</body>
</html>
```

2. Access the created page and check the output.

![console_deploy3.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_deploy3.png?api=v2)

## **Integration Example**

By executing the example of connecting to ALTIBASE through JNDI of the JDBC data source, it is checked whether the connection with ALTIBASE was successful.

### ALTIBASE Integration

Create a web application program that works with ALTIBASE to check the connection information.

1.Create singleVersion.jsp in the sample directory with the following contents.

```
<%@ page contentType="text/html;charset=euc-kr" pageEncoding="euc-kr"%>
<%@ page import="java.sql.*, javax.naming.*, javax.sql.*"%>

<head><title>Single Version Test Page</title></head>

<body>
<%
     Context    initCtx = new InitialContext();
     DataSource ds      = (DataSource)initCtx.lookup("altibase");
     Connection sCon    = ds.getConnection();
     Statement  sStmt   = sCon.createStatement();

     String query = "select '" +
                    "<b>DB name: </b>'||trim(db_name)||'<br>" +
                    "<b>version: </b>'||trim(product_signature)||'<br>" +
                    "<b>Current Time: </b>'"+
                    "||to_char(sysdate,'yyyy/mm/dd hh24:mi:ss')||'<hr>'" +
                    " from v$database;";

     ResultSet sRes = sStmt.executeQuery(query);
     sRes.next();
     out.println("<font size=4><b>ALTIBASE Connection Info</b></font><p>");
     out.println(sRes.getString(1));

     sRes.close();
     sStmt.close();
     sCon.close();
%>
</body>
</html>
```

2. Access the created page and check whether the information of the integrated Altibase target is displayed without error.

![console_deploy4.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_deploy4.png?api=v2)

### Integrating Different Versions of ALTIBASE

Create a web application program that works with ALTIBASE and ALTIBASE 5 at the same time to check the connection information.

1. Refer to "How to set the JDBC Driver to be used in WebLogic" and configure the JDBC driver files for ALTIBASE, ALTIBASE 5, and ALTIBASE 6 in advance so they can be used in WebLogic.

(ALTIBASE JDBC provides the same JDBC driver under a different name in each package version. It is prepared for easy use by copying from a higher version or lower version. In other words, to use ALTIBASE 5 and 6 versions simultaneously, the user can use the renamed version.

*The two drivers provided in the ALTIBASE package are the same driver with different names.

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ALTIBASE Version | ALTIBASE 5 | ALTIBASE 6 | ALTIBASE 7 |
| Current Package Version | Altibase.jar | Altibase.jar | Altibase.jar |
| Renamed version for compatibility | Altibase5.jar | Altibase6.jar | Altibase7.jar |

)

2. Create a JDBC data source for each. (JNDI makes it the same as the JDBC data source name.)

- JDBC data source altibase for ALTIBASE using Altibase.jar
  (Driver class name: Altibase.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver)
- JDBC data source altibase5 for ALTIBASE 5 using Altibase5.jar
  (Driver class name: Altibase5.jdbc.driver.AltibaseDriver)

![console_altibase5.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_altibase5.png?api=v2)

3. In the sample directory, create multiVersion.jsp with the following content.

```
<%@ page contentType="text/html;charset=euc-kr" pageEncoding="euc-kr"%>
<%@ page import="java.sql.*, javax.naming.*, javax.sql.*"%>

<head><title>Multi Version Test Page</title></head>

<body>
<%
     Context initCtx  = new InitialContext();
     DataSource ds1   = (DataSource)initCtx.lookup("altibase5");
     DataSource ds2   = (DataSource)initCtx.lookup("altibase6");
     Connection sCon1 = ds1.getConnection();
     Connection sCon2 = ds2.getConnection();
     Statement sStmt1 = sCon1.createStatement();
     Statement sStmt2 = sCon2.createStatement();

     String query = "select '" +
                    "<b>DB name: </b>'||trim(db_name)||'<br>" +
                    "<b>version: </b>'||trim(product_signature)||'<br>" +
                    "<b>Current Time: </b>'"+
                    "||to_char(sysdate,'yyyy/mm/dd hh24:mi:ss')||'<hr>'" +
                    " from v$database;";

     ResultSet sRes1 = sStmt1.executeQuery(query);
     ResultSet sRes2 = sStmt2.executeQuery(query);
     sRes1.next();
     sRes2.next();

     out.println("<font size=4><b>First ALTIBASE Connection Info.");
     out.println("</font></b><p>"+sRes1.getString(1));
     out.println("<font size=4><b>Second ALTIBASE Connection Info.");
     out.println("</font></b><p>"+sRes2.getString(1));

     sRes1.close();
     sRes2.close();
     sStmt1.close();
     sStmt2.close();
     sCon1.close();
     sCon2.close();
%>
</body>
</html>
```

4. Access to the created page and check whether the information of the integrating target Altibase is displayed without error.

![console_altibase5_2.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/3.%20ALTIBASE%20and%20WebLogic%20Integration/console_altibase5_2.png?api=v2)

# 4. Fail-Over & Load-Balancing Settings
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=14058337
Updated: 2025-09-24T09:10:43.000+0900

- [Setting in WebLogic](#id-4.Fail-Over&Load-BalancingSettings-SettinginWebLogic) - [Fail-Over](#id-4.Fail-Over&Load-BalancingSettings-Fail-Over) - [Load-Balancing](#id-4.Fail-Over&Load-BalancingSettings-Load-Balancing) - [Setting in ALTIBASE](#id-4.Fail-Over&Load-BalancingSettings-SettinginALTIBASE)

This chapter describes how to set up Fail-Over and Load-Balancing in WebLogic or Altibase.

## **Setting in WebLogic**

While creating multiple JDBC data sources, the user can set up either Fail-Over or Load-Balancing as an algorithm. For the setting method and details refer to the related document.

### Fail-Over

Proceed by sending the connection request to the first JDBC data source in the multiple JDBC data source list and, if the request fails, to the next JDBC data source. This process continues until a suitable connection is obtained or the end of the list is reached, and an exception is raised if the connection is not obtained until the end of the list.

### Load-Balancing

This evenly distributes connection requests to data sources in multiple JDBC data source lists. This algorithm basically provides a Fail-Over algorithm.

## **Setting in ALTIBASE**

Altibase v5.3.3 and later provides library-layer Fail-Over and Load-Balancing that can be used to integrate with WebLogic.

For setting method and details, please refer to "Altibase Replication Manual" and "Altibase JDBC Manual".
<!-- SOURCE_BLOCK_END source_id="AID-SRC-000411" block_id="BLOCK-000396" -->

# Integration Error
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/Integration+Error
Updated: 2025-09-24T09:11:18.000+0900

- [Cannot load driver](#IntegrationError-Cannotloaddriver) - [Can not make a database connection to the given URL / Invalid Altibase URL (No suitable driver)](#IntegrationError-CannotmakeadatabaseconnectiontothegivenURL/InvalidAltibaseURL(Nosuitabledriver)) - [Could not create pool connection](#IntegrationError-Couldnotcreatepoolconnection) - [Client unable to establish connection / Communication link failure](#IntegrationError-Clientunabletoestablishconnection/Communicationlinkfailure) - [Hang phenomenon](#IntegrationError-Hangphenomenon)

## Cannot load driver

This occurs when attempting to connect without the JDBC driver set up normally.

Refer to "How to set the JDBC Driver to be used in WebLogic."

## Can not make a database connection to the given URL / Invalid Altibase URL (No suitable driver)

If there is an error in the connection URL as below, an error occurs.

- Incorrect format, typo
- When JDBC item is set to a name other than "Altibase" (In this case, no suitable driver may occur depending on the version.)

```
jdbc:otherDBMS://127.0.0.1:20300/mydb
```

## Could not create pool connection

This occurs when there is an error in the connection pool configuration when creating a JDBC data source. There are various cases, but typical cases are as follows.

- When the connection target is ALTIBASE 4, the user to access in the form of "user=sys" must be entered in the property.

## Client unable to establish connection / Communication link failure

In the following cases, a client unable to establish a connection error occurs. (Communication link failure may occur depending on the version.)

- ALTIBASE server is not running
- If the connection is impossible because the IP address or port number of the ALTIBASE server is incorrectly set in the connection URL

The following is an example of the case where the IP address of the ALTIBASE server to be integrated is 192.168.1.81 and the port number is 20300, and it is incorrectly specified as a different value.

```
jdbc:Altibase://192.168.1.80:20800/mydb
```

## Hang phenomenon

If the user tries to connect while the ALTIBASE JDBC driver and the CM protocol version of the ALTIBASE server are different, a phenomenon such as hang may occur depending on the WebLogic version.

When this happens, most of the WebLogic server instances have to be restarted, so caution is required in advance.

For related information, refer to How to Check the ALTIBASE JDBC Driver Version.
<!-- SOURCE_BLOCK_END source_id="AID-SRC-000412" block_id="BLOCK-000397" -->

# WebLogic Glossary
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/WebLogic+Glossary
Updated: 2025-09-24T09:11:50.000+0900

- [Domain](#WebLogicGlossary-Domain) - [WebLogic Server Instance (Administration Server, Managed Server)](#WebLogicGlossary-WebLogicServerInstance(AdministrationServer,ManagedServer)) - [JDBC Data Source](#WebLogicGlossary-JDBCDataSource) - [Connection Pool](#WebLogicGlossary-ConnectionPool) - [Deployment & Distribution](#WebLogicGlossary-Deployment&Distribution)

Before integrating Altibase and WebLogic, this chapter briefly explains WebLogic and related terms.

### Domain

A domain is a logical grouping of WebLogic server instances. A domain consists of one or more WebLogic Server instances.

The user can configure multiple domains with one WebLogic (WebLogic Server/WLS) installation, or configure one domain from multiple WebLogic installations.

![weblogic_domain.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/WebLogic%20Glossary/weblogic_domain.png?api=v2)

### WebLogic Server Instance (Administration Server, Managed Server)

WebLogic server instance is a process that can deploy web application, web service, EJB, etc.

It is divided into "Administration Server" and "Managed Server".

![Weblogic_managed_server.png](https://docs.altibase.com/download/attachments/embedded-page/arch/WebLogic%20Glossary/Weblogic_managed_server.png?api=v2)

- Administration Server

  To manage the entire domain, the WebLogic server instance with the Administration Console deployed together is created when the domain is created.
- Managed Server

  All WebLogic Server instances except the administration server can be added separately or clustered between instances.

  That is, one domain consists of one Administration Server and zero or more Managed Servers.

### JDBC Data Source

A JDBC data source is the Java object for a WebLogic server instance to connect to the RDBMS.

When creating a JDBC data source for the RDBMS to be integrated, and specifying the WebLogic server instance to use the JDBC data source, the web application deployed in the WebLogic server instance works with the target RDBMS by specifying the JNDI name of the JDBC data source in the source code.

In order to create a JDBC data source, the relevant JDBC driver must be set in advance so that it can be used in WebLogic.

### Connection Pool

Connection set with RDBMS, which is automatically created when creating a JDBC data source, is adjusted by various properties such as "Initial Capacity" and "Maximum Capacity".

### Deployment & Distribution

Both deployment and distribution are synonymous for deploy and are unified as "deployment" in this document.
<!-- SOURCE_BLOCK_END source_id="AID-SRC-000413" block_id="BLOCK-000398" -->

Updated: 2020-05-15T15:48:45.000+0900

## Overview

This is a technical document for integrating with Altibase and WebLogic. It also covers running a simple web application that works with Altibase on the assumption that WebLogic is installed.

This document is based on WebLogic 12.1.3.0 on the Windows platform, and all contents may differ depending on the version. For basic environments such as WebLogic installation and domain creation, refer to Oracle's documentation and management console help provided when installing WebLogic (Administration Console).

[Oracle Documentation Library](http://docs.oracle.com/middleware/1213/wls/index.html)

In addition to this document, the documents to be referenced during development are as follows.

- JAVA Development Guide
- JBOSS Integration Guide for Altibase
- TOMCAT Integration Guide for Altibase
- WEBSPHERE Integration Guide for Altibase
- WEBLOGIC Integration Guide for Altibase
- Spring Integration Guide for Altibase
- HIBERNATE Integration Guide for Altibase
- iBatis Integration Guide for Altibase

For errors and improvements related to this document, please contact the technical support portal or technical support center.

- Technical support portal: [http://support.altibase.com](http://support.altibase.com/) > Technical Knowledge > Q&A
- Technical support center: 02-2082-1114

# WebSphere Integration Guide for Altibase
Source: https://docs.altibase.com/display/arch/WebSphere+Integration+Guide+for+Altibase
Updated: 2025-09-23T10:10:09.000+0900

## - [Overview](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-Overview) - [WebSphere Installation](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-WebSphereInstallation) - [Basic Installation](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-BasicInstallation) - [WebSphere Directory Structure](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-WebSphereDirectoryStructure) - [Starting WebSphere](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-StartingWebSphere) - [Shutting Down WebSphere](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-ShuttingDownWebSphere) - [JDBC Driver Settings](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-JDBCDriverSettings) - [Acquiring Altibase JDBC Driver](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-AcquiringAltibaseJDBCDriver) - [Checking Altibase JDBC Driver Version](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-CheckingAltibaseJDBCDriverVersion) - [Applying JDBC Driver](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-ApplyingJDBCDriver) - [Altibase and WebSphere Integration (AltibaseConnectionPool)](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-AltibaseandWebSphereIntegration(AltibaseConnectionPool)) - [JDBC Provider Settings](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-JDBCProviderSettings) - [Data Source Settings](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-DataSourceSettings) - [Application Registration and Setting](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-ApplicationRegistrationandSetting) - [Integration Test](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-IntegrationTest) - [FailOver Configuration](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-FailOverConfiguration) - [FailOver](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-FailOver) - [FailOver Related Properties](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-FailOverRelatedProperties) - [Applying FailOver](#WebSphereIntegrationGuideforAltibase-ApplyingFailOver)

## Overview

This document is a guide for operating Altibase and WebSphere. This document describes how to install WebSphere, how to set environment variables, and how to integrate Altibase and WebSphere.

This document is based on Altibase v7.1.0 and WebSphere v9.0.

For errors and improvements related to this document, please contact the technical support portal or technical support center.

- Technical support portal: [http://support.altibase.com](http://support.altibase.com/) > Technical Knowledge > Q&A
- Technical support center: 02-2082-1114

## WebSphere Installation

This chapter describes the process of downloading and installing WebSphere, the directory structure of WebSphere, and describes how to start and shut down WebSphere.

### Basic Installation

Download WebSphere package.

To download WebSphere, IBM Installation Manager must be installed first.

(This document is based on IBM Installation Manager version 1.8.5.)

The link to download IBM Installation Manager is:
